#### PSP-2000 and PSP-3000 models

The PSP-2000 (also known as the Slim & Lite in PAL territories) was the first major hardware revision of the PlayStation Portable, released in September [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_in_video_gaming "2007 in video gaming"). The 2000 series was 33% lighter and 19% slimmer than the original PlayStation Portable.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-SonyE3-98)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-99) The capacity of the battery was also reduced by ⅓ but the run time remained the same as the previous model due to lower power consumption. Older model batteries will still work and they extend the amount of playing time.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-100) The PSP Slim & Lite has a new gloss finish. Its serial port was also modified to accommodate a new video-out feature (while rendering older PSP remote controls incompatible). On a PSP-2000, PSP games will only output to external monitors or TVs in progressive scan mode, so that televisions incapable of supporting progressive scan will not display PSP games; non-game video will output in either progressive or interlaced mode. [USB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USB "USB") charging was also made possible.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-101) Buttons are also reportedly more responsive on the PSP-2000.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-102) In [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_in_video_gaming "2008 in video gaming"), Sony released a second hardware revision called the PSP-3000 which included several features that were not present in the PSP-2000, such as a built-in microphone and upgraded screen, as well as the ability to output PSP games in interlaced mode.

#### PSP Go model

Released in October [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_video_gaming "2009 in video gaming"), the PSP Go diverged from the original design of the previous models in multiple facets. Unlike previous PSP models, the PSP Go does not feature a UMD drive but instead has 16[GB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigabyte "Gigabyte") of internal [flash memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_memory "Flash memory") to store games, videos and other media.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-Announcement-103) This can be extended by up to 32 GB with the use of a [Memory Stick Micro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_Stick_Micro "Memory Stick Micro") (M2) flash card. Also unlike previous PSP models, the PSP Go's rechargeable battery is not removable or replaceable by the user. The unit is 43% lighter and 56% smaller than the original PSP-1000,[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-kotaku_announce-104) and 16% lighter and 35% smaller than the PSP-3000.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-TSA-105) It has a 3.8" 480×272 [LCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid-crystal_display "Liquid-crystal display")[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PlayStation-106) (compared to the larger 4.3" 480×272 pixel LCD on previous PSP models).[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-107) The screen slides up to reveal the main controls. The overall shape and sliding mechanism are similar to that of Sony's [mylo COM-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mylo_(Sony) "Mylo (Sony)") internet device.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-Giz-108) The PSP Go was produced and sold concurrently with its predecessor the PSP-3000 although it did not replace it.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-kotaku_announce-104) All games on the PSP Go must be purchased and downloaded from the [PlayStation Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Store "PlayStation Store") as the handheld is not compatible with the original PSP's physical media, the Universal Media Disc. The handheld also features connectivity with the [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3")'s controllers the [Sixaxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixaxis "Sixaxis") and [DualShock 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualShock_3 "DualShock 3") via [Bluetooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth "Bluetooth") connection.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-TSA-105)

#### PSP Street

### PlayStation Vita

Main article: [PlayStation Vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Vita "PlayStation Vita")

Released in Japan on December 17, 2011, and North America on February 22, 2012,[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-111) the PlayStation Vita[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-112) was previously codenamed _Next Generation Portable_ (_NGP_). It was officially unveiled by Sony on January 27, 2011, at the PlayStation Meeting 2011.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-113) The original model of the handheld, the PCH-1000 series features a 5-inch OLED touchscreen,[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-114) two analog sticks, a rear touchpad, Sixaxis motion sensing and a 4 core ARM Cortex-A9 MPCore processor.

The new PCH-2000 series system is a lighter redesign of the device that was announced at the SCEJA Press Conference in September 2013 prior to the Tokyo Game Show. This model is 20% thinner and 15% lighter compared to the original model, has an additional hour of battery life, an LCD instead of OLED, includes a micro USB Type B port, and 1 GB of internal storage memory. It was released in Japan on October 10, 2013, in six colors: white, black, pink, yellow, blue, and olive green, and in North America on May 6, 2014.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-115)

The Vita was discontinued in March 2019. SIE president Jim Ryan said that while the Vita was a great device, they have moved away from portable consoles, "clearly it's a business that we're no longer in now".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-gi_first_25-13)

#### PlayStation TV

Main article: [PlayStation TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_TV "PlayStation TV")

PlayStation TV, known in Asia as PlayStation Vita TV or PS Vita TV, is a [microconsole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microconsole "Microconsole") and a non-portable variant of the PlayStation Vita handheld. It was announced on September 9, 2013, at a Sony Computer Entertainment Japan presentation. Instead of featuring a display screen, the console connects to a television via HDMI. Users can play using a Sixaxis or a DualShock 3 controller, although due to the difference in features between the controller and the handheld, certain games are not compatible with PS TV, such as those that are dependent on the system's touchscreen, rear touchpad, microphone or camera. The device is said to be compatible with over 100 Vita games, as well as various digital PlayStation Portable, PlayStation and PC Engine titles. The system supports Remote Play compatibility with the PlayStation 4, allowing players to stream games from the PS4 to a separate TV connected to PS TV, and also allows users to stream content from video services such as Hulu and Niconico, as well as access the PlayStation Store. The system was released in Japan on November 14, 2013, in North America on October 14, 2014, and in Europe and Australasia on November 14, 2014.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-116)

**PlayStation**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-1) is a [video gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game")[brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand "Brand") owned and produced by [Sony Interactive Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment") (SIE), a subsidiary of Japanese conglomerate [Sony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony "Sony"). The brand is recognized primarily for its series of [home video game consoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_video_game_console "Home video game console"), though it also includes [handheld devices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handheld_game_console "Handheld game console"), online services, and other media products.

The brainchild of Sony executive [Ken Kutaragi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Kutaragi "Ken Kutaragi"), the brand began with the [first PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)") home console released in Japan in 1994 and worldwide the following year, which became the first console of any type to ship over 100 million units, which made PlayStation a globally recognized brand.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-100Mrecord2-2) Since then there have been numerous newer consoles—the most recent being the [PlayStation 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_5 "PlayStation 5") released in 2020—while there have also been a series of handheld consoles and a number of other electronics such as a [media center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_theater_PC "Home theater PC") and a [smartphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smartphone "Smartphone"). The main series of controllers utilized by the PlayStation series is the [DualShock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualShock "DualShock"), a line of [vibration-feedback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haptic_technology "Haptic technology")[gamepads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamepad "Gamepad").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-3) SIE also operate numerous online services like [PlayStation Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Network "PlayStation Network"), the [PlayStation Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Store "PlayStation Store"), and the subscription-based [PlayStation Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Plus "PlayStation Plus"), which may also offer non-gaming entertainment services; the PlayStation Network has over 103 million active users monthly as of December 2019.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-sie200107-4)

The series also has a strong line-up of first-party games due to [PlayStation Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Studios "PlayStation Studios"), a group of many studios owned by Sony Interactive Entertainment that exclusively developed them for PlayStation consoles. In addition, the series features various budget re-releases of games by Sony with different names for each region; these include the [PlayStation Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Hits "PlayStation Hits"), [Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essentials_(PlayStation) "Essentials (PlayStation)"), [Essentials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essentials_(PlayStation) "Essentials (PlayStation)"), and [The Best](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_(PlayStation) "The Best (PlayStation)") selection of games. It is also known for the four iconic PlayStation face buttons ([![Image 6: Triangle](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/PlayStationTriangle.svg/20px-PlayStationTriangle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PlayStationTriangle.svg "Triangle"), [![Image 7: Cross](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/PlayStationCircle.svg/20px-PlayStationCircle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PlayStationCircle.svg "Circle"), [![Image 8: X](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/PlayStationCross.svg/20px-PlayStationCross.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PlayStationCross.svg "X"), [![Image 9: Square](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/PlayStationSquare.svg/20px-PlayStationSquare.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PlayStationSquare.svg "Square")) and has been known for its numerous marketing campaigns, the latest of which being the "Play Has No Limits" commercials.

### Origins

Further information: [Timeline of early 3D computer graphics hardware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_early_3D_computer_graphics_hardware "Timeline of early 3D computer graphics hardware")

PlayStation was the brainchild of [Ken Kutaragi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Kutaragi "Ken Kutaragi"), a [Sony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony "Sony") executive who managed one of the company's hardware engineering divisions and was later dubbed "The Father of the PlayStation".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-6)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Nintendo_Playstation_Prototype_%2826398121058%29.jpg/250px-Nintendo_Playstation_Prototype_%2826398121058%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nintendo_Playstation_Prototype_(26398121058).jpg)

One of two known remaining prototypes of Sony's original "PlayStation", a [Super NES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_NES "Super NES") with a [built-in CD-ROM drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_NES_CD-ROM "Super NES CD-ROM")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-7)

Until 1991, Sony had little direct involvement with the video game industry. The company supplied components for other consoles, such as the sound chip for the [Super Famicom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Nintendo_Entertainment_System "Super Nintendo Entertainment System") from Nintendo, and operated a video game studio, [Sony Imagesoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Imagesoft "Sony Imagesoft").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-8) As part of a joint project between Nintendo and Sony that began as early as 1988, the two companies worked to create a [CD-ROM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD-ROM "CD-ROM") version of the Super Famicom,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-9) though Nintendo denied the existence of the Sony deal as late as March 1991.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-cgw199106-10) At the [Consumer Electronics Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_Electronics_Show "Consumer Electronics Show") in June 1991, Sony revealed a Super Famicom with a built-in CD-ROM drive that incorporated [Green Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Book_(CD_standard) "Green Book (CD standard)") technology or CD-i, called "Play Station" (also known as [SNES-CD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNES-CD "SNES-CD")). However, a day after the announcement at CES, Nintendo announced that it would be breaking its partnership with Sony, opting to go with [Philips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philips "Philips") instead but using the same technology.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-History-11) The deal was broken by Nintendo after they were unable to agree on how revenue would be split between the two companies.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-History-11) The breaking of the partnership infuriated Sony President [Norio Ohga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norio_Ohga "Norio Ohga"), who responded by appointing Kutaragi with the responsibility of developing the PlayStation project to rival Nintendo.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-History-11)

At that time, negotiations were still ongoing between Nintendo and Sony, with Nintendo offering Sony a "non-gaming role" regarding their new partnership with Philips. This proposal was swiftly rejected by Kutaragi who was facing increasing criticism over his work with regard to entering the video game industry from within Sony. Negotiations officially ended in May 1992 and in order to decide the fate of the PlayStation project, a meeting was held in June 1992, consisting of Sony President Ohga, PlayStation Head Kutaragi and several senior members of Sony's board. At the meeting, Kutaragi unveiled a proprietary CD-ROM-based system he had been working on which involved playing video games with 3D graphics to the board. Eventually, Sony President Ohga decided to retain the project after being reminded by Kutaragi of the humiliation he suffered from Nintendo. Nevertheless, due to strong opposition from a majority present at the meeting as well as widespread internal opposition to the project by the older generation of Sony executives, Kutaragi and his team had to be shifted from Sony's headquarters to [Sony Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music"), a completely separate financial entity owned by Sony, so as to retain the project and maintain relationships with Philips for the MMCD development project (which helped lead to the creation of the [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD")).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-History-11)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Playstation_logo_colour.svg/250px-Playstation_logo_colour.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Playstation_logo_colour.svg)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/PlayStation_logo.svg/250px-PlayStation_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PlayStation_logo.svg)

Original PlayStation logo introduced in 1994 (left); this version had been primarily marketed until the introduction of a monochrome variant in 2009 (right)

According to SCE's producer Ryoji Akagawa and chairman [Shigeo Maruyama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeo_Maruyama "Shigeo Maruyama"), there was uncertainty over whether the console should primarily focus on [2D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2D_computer_graphics "2D computer graphics")[sprite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprite_(computer_graphics) "Sprite (computer graphics)") graphics or [3D polygon graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics"). Eventually, after witnessing the success of [Sega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sega "Sega")'s _[Virtua Fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtua\_Fighter\_(video\_game) "Virtua Fighter (video game)")_ in Japanese arcades, Sony realized "the direction of the PlayStation became instantly clear" and 3D polygon graphics became the console's primary focus.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-12)

The PlayStation logo was designed by Manabu Sakamoto. He wanted the logo to capture the 3D support of the console, but instead of just adding apparent depth to the letters "P" and "S", he created an [optical illusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_illusion "Optical illusion") that suggested the letters in depth of space. Sakamoto also stuck with four bright principal colors, red, yellow, green, and blue, only having to tune the green color for better harmony across the logo. Sakamoto also designed the black-and-white logo based on the same design, reserved for times where colors could not be used.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-gi_first_25-13)

### Formation of Sony Computer Entertainment

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Sony_Computer_Entertainment_logo_%28No_Trademark%29.svg/250px-Sony_Computer_Entertainment_logo_%28No_Trademark%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sony_Computer_Entertainment_logo_(No_Trademark).svg)

Sony Computer Entertainment logo (1993–2016)

At [Sony Music Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Entertainment "Sony Music Entertainment"), Kutaragi worked closely with [Shigeo Maruyama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeo_Maruyama "Shigeo Maruyama"), the CEO of Sony Music, and with Akira Sato to form Sony Computer Entertainment Inc. (SCEI) on November 16, 1993.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-scei-history-14) A building block of SCEI was its initial partnership with Sony Music which helped SCEI attract creative talent to the company as well as assist SCEI in manufacturing, marketing and producing discs, something that Sony Music had been doing with Music Discs. The final two key members of SCEI were Terry Tokunaka, the president of SCEI from Sony's headquarters, and [Olaf Olafsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olaf_Olafsson "Olaf Olafsson"). Olafsson was CEO and president of New York-based Sony Interactive Entertainment[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-15) which was the parent company for the 1994-founded Sony Computer Entertainment of America (SCEA).

The PlayStation project, SCEI's first official project, was finally given the green light by Sony executives in 1993 after a few years of development. Also in 1993, [Phil Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Harrison "Phil Harrison"), who later became President of [SCE Worldwide Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIE_Worldwide_Studios "SIE Worldwide Studios"), was recruited into SCEI to attract developers and publishers to produce games for their new PlayStation platform.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-History-11)

In March 1994, _[Computer Gaming World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer\_Gaming\_World "Computer Gaming World")_ reported a rumor that the "**Sony PS-X**" would be released in Japan "before the end of this year and will retail for less than $400".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-cgw199403-16) After a demonstration of Sony's distribution plan as well as tech demos of its new console to game publishers and developers in a hotel in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") in 1994, numerous developers began to approach PlayStation. Two of whom later became major partners were [Electronic Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts "Electronic Arts") in the West and [Namco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namco "Namco") in Japan. One of the factors that attracted developers to the platform was the use of a 3D-capable, CD-ROM-based console that was much cheaper and easier to manufacture compared to Nintendo's rival console, which used cartridge systems. The project eventually hit Japanese stores in December 1994 and gained massive sales due to its lower price point than its competitor, the [Sega Saturn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sega_Saturn "Sega Saturn"). The popularity of the console spread after its release worldwide in North America and Europe.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-History-11)

## Home consoles

### PlayStation

Main article: [PlayStation (console)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)")

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/PlayStation-SCPH-1000-with-Controller.jpg/250px-PlayStation-SCPH-1000-with-Controller.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PlayStation-SCPH-1000-with-Controller.jpg)

Original PlayStation with a [controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_controller "PlayStation controller")

The original PlayStation, released in Japan on December 3, [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_in_video_gaming "1994 in video gaming"), was the first of the PlayStation series of console and hand-held game devices. It has included successor consoles and upgrades including the [Net Yaroze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_Yaroze "Net Yaroze") (a special black PlayStation with tools and instructions to program PlayStation games and applications), "PS one" (a smaller version of the original) and the [PocketStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PocketStation "PocketStation") (a handheld which enhances PlayStation games and also acts as a memory card). It was part of the [fifth generation of video game consoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_generation_of_video_game_consoles "Fifth generation of video game consoles") competing against the [Sega Saturn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sega_Saturn "Sega Saturn") and the [Nintendo 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_64 "Nintendo 64"). By December 2003, the PlayStation and PS one had shipped a combined total of 102.49 million units,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-ps1shipments-17) eventually becoming the first video game console to sell 120 million units.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-100Mrecord-18)

#### PS One

Main article: [PlayStation models §PS One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_models#PS_One "PlayStation models")

Released on July 7, [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_in_video_gaming "2000 in video gaming"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-19) concurrently with its successor the PlayStation 2, the PS One (stylized as PS one) was a considerably smaller, redesigned version of the original PlayStation video game console.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PSOne-20) The PS one went on to outsell all other consoles, including its successor, throughout the remainder of the year.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PSOne-20) It featured two main changes from its predecessor, the first being a cosmetic change to the console and the second being the home menu's [graphical user interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphical_user_interface "Graphical user interface") (GUI); a variation of the GUI previously used only on PAL consoles up to that point.

### PlayStation 2

Main article: PlayStation 2

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Sony-PlayStation-2-30001-wController-L.jpg/250px-Sony-PlayStation-2-30001-wController-L.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sony-PlayStation-2-30001-wController-L.jpg)

Original PlayStation 2 with a [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") disc drive and a [DualShock 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualShock#DualShock_2 "DualShock") controller

Released in [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_in_video_gaming "2000 in video gaming"), 15 months after the [Dreamcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamcast "Dreamcast") and a year before its other competitors, the [Xbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_(console) "Xbox (console)") and the [GameCube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube "GameCube"), the PlayStation 2 is part of the [sixth generation of video game consoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_video_game_consoles_(sixth_generation) "History of video game consoles (sixth generation)"), and is [backwards-compatible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backwards-compatible "Backwards-compatible") with most original PlayStation games. Like its predecessor, it has received a slimmer redesign. It is the [most successful console](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_million-selling_game_consoles "List of million-selling game consoles") in the world,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-21) having sold over 155 million units as of December 28, 2012.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-autogenerated3-22) On November 29, 2005, the PS2 became the fastest game console to reach 100 million units shipped, accomplishing the feat within 5 years and 9 months from its launch. This achievement occurred faster than its predecessor, the PlayStation, which took "9 years and 6 months since launch" to reach the same figure.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-100Mrecord-18) PlayStation 2 shipments in Japan ended on December 28, 2012.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-famitsu-23)_The Guardian_ reported on January 4, 2013, that PS2 production had ended worldwide, but studies showed that many people all around the world still own one even if it is no longer in use. PlayStation 2 has been ranked as the best-selling console of all time as of 2015.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-Guardian_end-24)

#### Slimline model

Main article: [PlayStation 2 models §Slimline case designs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_2_models#Slimline_case_designs "PlayStation 2 models")

Released in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_in_video_gaming "2004 in video gaming"), four years after the launch of the original PlayStation 2, the PlayStation 2 Slimline was the first major redesign of the PlayStation 2. Compared to its predecessor, the Slimline was smaller, thinner, quieter and also included a built-in [Ethernet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethernet "Ethernet") port (in some markets it also has an integrated [modem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modem "Modem")). In [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_in_video_gaming "2007 in video gaming"), Sony began shipping a revision of the Slimline which was lighter than the original Slimline together with a lighter [AC adapter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_adapter "AC adapter").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-ign-lighterPS2-25) In [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_in_video_gaming "2008 in video gaming"), Sony released yet another revision of the Slimline which had an overhauled internal design incorporating the power supply into the console itself like the original PlayStation 2 resulting in a further reduced total weight of the console.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-26)

### PlayStation 3

Main article: [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Sony-PlayStation-3-CECHA01-wController-L.jpg/250px-Sony-PlayStation-3-CECHA01-wController-L.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sony-PlayStation-3-CECHA01-wController-L.jpg)

Original PlayStation 3 console with a [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") disc drive and a [DualShock 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualShock_3 "DualShock 3") controller

Released on November 11, 2006, in Japan, the PlayStation 3 (PS3) is a [seventh generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_video_game_consoles_(seventh_generation) "History of video game consoles (seventh generation)") game console from Sony. It competes with the [Microsoft Xbox 360](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360 "Xbox 360") and the Nintendo Wii. The PS3 is the first console in the series to introduce the use of [motion-sensing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_detection "Motion detection") technology through its [Sixaxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixaxis "Sixaxis") wireless controller. The console also incorporates a [Blu-ray Disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray_Disc "Blu-ray Disc") player and features [high-definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_video "High-definition video") resolution. The PS3 was originally offered with either a 20 GB or 60 GB hard drive, but over the years its capacity increased in increments available up to 500 GB. The PlayStation 3 has sold over 80 million consoles worldwide as of November 2013.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-WorldPS3Sales-27)

#### Slim model

Like its predecessors, the PlayStation 3 was re-released in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_video_gaming "2009 in video gaming") as a "slim" model. The redesigned model is 33% smaller, 36% lighter, and consumes 34% to 45% less power than previous models.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PS3SlimSpecs-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-29) In addition, it features a redesigned cooling system and a smaller [Cell processor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_processor "Cell processor") which was moved to a [45nm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/45nm "45nm") manufacturing process.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-ArsTechnicaInterview-30) It sold in excess of a million units within its first 3 weeks on sale.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-31) The redesign added support for [CEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-Definition_Multimedia_Interface#CEC "High-Definition Multimedia Interface") (branded as BRAVIA Sync, VIERA Link, and others), allowing console control via a TV remote. The PS3 slim also runs quieter and is cooler than previous models due to its 45 nm Cell. The PS3 Slim no longer has the "main power" switch (similar to [PlayStation 2 slim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slim_PlayStation_2 "Slim PlayStation 2")), like the previous PS3 models, which was located at the back of the console.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PS3SlimSpecs-28) It was officially released on September 1, 2009, in North America and Europe and on September 3, 2009, in Japan, Australia and New Zealand.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PS3SlimSpecs-28)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PS3SlimPressReleaseAU-32)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-33)

#### Super Slim model

In 2012, Sony revealed a new "Super Slim" PlayStation 3. The new console, with a completely redesigned case that has a sliding door covering the disc drive (which has been moved to the top of the console), is 4.3 pounds, almost three pounds lighter than the previous "slim" model. The console comes with either 12 GB flash memory or a 250 GB, 500 GB hard drive. Several bundles which include a Super Slim PS3 and a selection of games are available.

### PlayStation 4

Main article: [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4")

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/PS4-Console-wDS4.jpg/250px-PS4-Console-wDS4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PS4-Console-wDS4.jpg)

Original PlayStation 4 with a Blu-ray disc drive and a [DualShock 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualShock#DualShock_4 "DualShock") controller

The [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") (PS4) was announced by [Sony Computer Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Computer_Entertainment "Sony Computer Entertainment") at a press conference on February 20, 2013. In the meeting, Sony revealed some hardware specifications of the new console.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PS4_announcement-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PS4_announced_-_TechRadar-35) It introduced the [x86](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X86 "X86") architecture to the PlayStation series. According to lead system architect Mark Cerny, development on the PlayStation 4 began as early as 2008.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PS4_announced_-_IGN-36) PlayStation Europe CEO Jim Ryan emphasized in 2011 that Sony wanted to avoid launching the next-generation console behind the competition.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-37)

Among the new applications and services, Sony introduced the PlayStation App, allowing PS4 owners to turn smartphones and tablets into a [second screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_screen "Second screen") to enhance gameplay.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-SCE_introduces_PS4-38) The company also planned to debut [PlayStation Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Now "PlayStation Now") game streaming service, powered by technology from [Gaikai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaikai "Gaikai").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-40) By incorporating a share button on the new controller and making it possible to view in-game content being streamed live from friends, Sony planned to place more focus on social gameplay as well.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-SCE_introduces_PS4-38) The PlayStation 4 was first released in North America on November 15, 2013. As part of the [eighth generation of video game consoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_video_game_consoles_(eighth_generation) "History of video game consoles (eighth generation)"), it competes with Microsoft's [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One") and Nintendo's [Wii U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U "Wii U") and [Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch").

#### Slim model

**PlayStation 4 Slim** (officially marketed simply as **PlayStation 4** or **PS4**) was unveiled on September 7, 2016. It is a revision of the original PS4 hardware with a streamlined form factor. The new casing is 40% smaller and carries a rounded body with a matte finish on the top of the console rather than a two-tone finish. The two USB ports on the front have a larger gap between them, and the optical audio port was also removed.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-168 "PlayStation 4") It ships with a minor update to the DualShock 4 controller, with the light bar visible through the top of the touchpad and a dark matte grey coloured exterior instead of a partially shiny black. The PS4 Slim was released on September 15, 2016, with a 500 GB model at the same price point as the original PS4 model.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-ars-ps4slim-169 "PlayStation 4") Its model number is CUH-2000.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-ps4pro_model_no-170 "PlayStation 4")

#### Pro model

**PlayStation 4 Pro** or **PS4 Pro** for short (originally announced under the codename **Neo**)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-PS4Neo-35 "PlayStation 4") was unveiled on September 7, 2016. Its model number is CUH-7000.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-ps4pro_model_no-170 "PlayStation 4") It is an updated version of the PlayStation 4 with improved hardware, including an upgraded GPU with 4.2 teraflops of processing power, and a higher CPU clock. It is designed primarily to enable selected games to be playable at [4K resolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4K_resolution "4K resolution"), and improved quality for [PlayStation VR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_VR "PlayStation VR"). All games are backwards and forward compatible between PS4 and PS4 Pro, but games with optimizations will have improved graphics performance on PS4 Pro. Although capable of streaming 4K video from online sources, PS4 Pro does not support [Ultra HD Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_HD_Blu-ray "Ultra HD Blu-ray").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-verge-no4kbluray-171 "PlayStation 4")[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-verge-ps4pro-172 "PlayStation 4")[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-engadget-pro-173 "PlayStation 4") Additionally the PS4 Pro is the only PS4 model which can remote play at 1080p. The other models are limited to 720p.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4#cite_note-sony_ps4_website-174 "PlayStation 4")

### PlayStation 5

Main article: [PlayStation 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_5 "PlayStation 5")

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Black_and_white_Playstation_5_base_edition_with_controller.png/250px-Black_and_white_Playstation_5_base_edition_with_controller.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Black_and_white_Playstation_5_base_edition_with_controller.png)

Original PlayStation 5 with a [4K Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_HD_Blu-ray "Ultra HD Blu-ray") disc drive and a [DualSense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualSense "DualSense") controller

The PlayStation 5 (PS5)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-2019-10-08_GameSpot-41) was released worldwide on November 12, 2020, and, alongside the [Xbox Series X and Series S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_Series_S "Xbox Series X and Series S"), released the same month, is part of the [ninth generation of video game consoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninth_generation_of_video_game_consoles "Ninth generation of video game consoles"). The first news of the PS5 came from [Mark Cerny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Cerny "Mark Cerny") in an interview with _[Wired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wired\_(magazine) "Wired (magazine)")_ in April 2019.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_april2019-42) Sony intended for the PlayStation 5 to be its next-generation console and planned to ship it worldwide by the end of 2020.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_oct2019-43) In early 2019, Sony's financial report for the quarter ending March 31, 2019, affirmed that new next-generation hardware was in development but would ship no earlier than April 2020.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-44)

The current specifications were released in October 2019.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-sieannounce-45) The console uses an 8-core, [16-thread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simultaneous_multithreading "Simultaneous multithreading") CPU based on AMD's [Zen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zen_2 "Zen 2") microarchitecture, manufactured on the [7 nanometer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_nanometer "7 nanometer") process node. The graphics processor is a custom variant of AMD's Navi family using the [RDNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RDNA_(microarchitecture) "RDNA (microarchitecture)") microarchitecture, which includes support for [hardware acceleration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardware_acceleration "Hardware acceleration") of [ray-tracing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_tracing_(graphics) "Ray tracing (graphics)") rendering, enabling real-time ray-traced graphics.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-sieannounce-45) The new console ships with a custom [SSD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_drive "Solid-state drive") storage, as Cerny emphasized the need for fast loading times and higher bandwidth to make games more immersive, as well as to support the required content streaming from disc for [8K resolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8K_resolution "8K resolution").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_april2019-42) In a second interview with Wired in October 2019, further details of the new hardware were revealed: the console's integrated [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") drive would support 100 GB Blu-ray discs[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_oct2019-43) and [Ultra HD Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_HD_Blu-ray "Ultra HD Blu-ray");[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-46) while a game installation from a disc is mandatory as to take advantage of the SSD, the user will have some fine-grain control of how much they want to have installed, such as only installing multiplayer components of a game.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_oct2019-43) Sony is developing an improved suspended gameplay state for the PlayStation 5 to consume less energy than the PlayStation 4.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-47)

The system's new controller, the [DualSense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualSense "DualSense") has adaptive triggers that can change the resistance to the player as necessary, such as changing the resistance during the action of pulling an arrow back in a bow in-game.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_oct2019-43) The controller also has strong [haptic feedback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haptic_technology "Haptic technology") through [voice coil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice_coil "Voice coil") actuators, which together with an improved controller speaker is intended to give better in-game feedback.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_oct2019-43)[USB-C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USB-C "USB-C") connectivity, together with a higher-rated battery are other improvements to the new controller.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_oct2019-43)

The PlayStation 5 features a completely revamped [user interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_interface "User interface").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-2019-10-08_GameSpot-41) The PlayStation 5 is backwards-compatible with most PlayStation 4 and PlayStation [VR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_reality "Virtual reality") games, with Cerny stating that the transition to the new console is meant to be a soft one.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-wired_ps5_april2019-42)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-sieannounce-45) In a later interview, Jim Ryan talked of the PlayStation 5 being able to play "99%" of PlayStation 4 games, an estimate derived from a sample size of "thousands".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-48)

#### Slim model

A revised slimmer design for the PS5, similar to past "slim" rereleases, was released in October 2023. Besides the slimmer design, the slim model features 1 TB of internal storage and replaces one of the USB-A ports with USB-C. The base version also removes the internal optical disc drive, replaced by an external drive.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-49)

#### Pro model

The PlayStation 5 Pro was released in November 2024. It features three main upgrades over the base PS5 model: a GPU that was about 45% faster than the base PS5 GPU, the inclusion of an [image upscaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_upscaling "Image upscaling") technology called PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), and an increase of internal storage to 2 TB.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-verge_pro_features-50)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-51) Games are able to take advantage of the improved graphical performance if programmed for it, with about 50 games ready to use this feature at launch.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-verge_pro_features-50)

## Handheld consoles

### PocketStation

Main article: [PocketStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PocketStation "PocketStation")

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Sony-PocketStation.jpg/250px-Sony-PocketStation.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sony-PocketStation.jpg)

PocketStation

The PocketStation is a Memory Card [peripheral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral "Peripheral") by Sony Computer Entertainment for the original [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)"). Categorized by Sony as a combination of a Memory Card and a miniature [personal digital assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_digital_assistant "Personal digital assistant").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-Pocketstation-90) Released exclusively in Japan on January 23, 1999,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-91) it featured a monochrome [LCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_crystal_display "Liquid crystal display"), a speaker, a [real-time clock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_clock "Real-time clock") and infrared communication capability. It could also be used as a standard PlayStation memory card by connecting it to a PlayStation memory card slot.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-Pocketstation-90) As a handheld device, it allowed users to play minigames downloaded from compatible PlayStation discs on the go. Over 80 PlayStation games featured integration with the peripheral, allowing players to download exclusive minigames, train characters, or unlock special items for titles like Final Fantasy VIII, Street Fighter Alpha 3, and Ridge Racer Type 4. It was extremely popular in Japan and Sony originally had plans to release it in the United States but the plan was ultimately scrapped due to various manufacturing and supply-and-demand problems.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-92)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-93)

#### PSP-2000 and PSP-3000 models

The PSP-2000 (also known as the Slim & Lite in PAL territories) was the first major hardware revision of the PlayStation Portable, released in September [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_in_video_gaming "2007 in video gaming"). The 2000 series was 33% lighter and 19% slimmer than the original PlayStation Portable.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-SonyE3-98)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-99) The capacity of the battery was also reduced by ⅓ but the run time remained the same as the previous model due to lower power consumption. Older model batteries will still work and they extend the amount of playing time.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-100) The PSP Slim & Lite has a new gloss finish. Its serial port was also modified to accommodate a new video-out feature (while rendering older PSP remote controls incompatible). On a PSP-2000, PSP games will only output to external monitors or TVs in progressive scan mode, so that televisions incapable of supporting progressive scan will not display PSP games; non-game video will output in either progressive or interlaced mode. [USB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USB "USB") charging was also made possible.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-101) Buttons are also reportedly more responsive on the PSP-2000.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-102) In [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_in_video_gaming "2008 in video gaming"), Sony released a second hardware revision called the PSP-3000 which included several features that were not present in the PSP-2000, such as a built-in microphone and upgraded screen, as well as the ability to output PSP games in interlaced mode.

#### PSP Go model

Released in October [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_in_video_gaming "2009 in video gaming"), the PSP Go diverged from the original design of the previous models in multiple facets. Unlike previous PSP models, the PSP Go does not feature a UMD drive but instead has 16[GB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigabyte "Gigabyte") of internal [flash memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_memory "Flash memory") to store games, videos and other media.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-Announcement-103) This can be extended by up to 32 GB with the use of a [Memory Stick Micro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_Stick_Micro "Memory Stick Micro") (M2) flash card. Also unlike previous PSP models, the PSP Go's rechargeable battery is not removable or replaceable by the user. The unit is 43% lighter and 56% smaller than the original PSP-1000,[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-kotaku_announce-104) and 16% lighter and 35% smaller than the PSP-3000.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-TSA-105) It has a 3.8" 480×272 [LCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid-crystal_display "Liquid-crystal display")[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-PlayStation-106) (compared to the larger 4.3" 480×272 pixel LCD on previous PSP models).[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-107) The screen slides up to reveal the main controls. The overall shape and sliding mechanism are similar to that of Sony's [mylo COM-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mylo_(Sony) "Mylo (Sony)") internet device.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-Giz-108) The PSP Go was produced and sold concurrently with its predecessor the PSP-3000 although it did not replace it.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-kotaku_announce-104) All games on the PSP Go must be purchased and downloaded from the [PlayStation Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Store "PlayStation Store") as the handheld is not compatible with the original PSP's physical media, the Universal Media Disc. The handheld also features connectivity with the [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3")'s controllers the [Sixaxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixaxis "Sixaxis") and [DualShock 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DualShock_3 "DualShock 3") via [Bluetooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth "Bluetooth") connection.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-TSA-105)

#### PSP Street

The PSP Street (also known as the PSP-E1000) is a budget-focused PSP model which, unlike previous PSP models, does not feature [Wi-Fi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wi-Fi "Wi-Fi") or stereo speakers (replaced by a single mono speaker)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-109) and has a matte "charcoal black" finish similar to the slim PlayStation 3.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-E1000-110) The E1000 was announced at [Gamescom 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamescom#Gamescom_2011 "Gamescom") and available across the [PAL region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PAL_region "PAL region") for an RRP of [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")99.99.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-E1000-110)

### PlayStation Vita

Main article: [PlayStation Vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Vita "PlayStation Vita")

Released in Japan on December 17, 2011, and North America on February 22, 2012,[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-111) the PlayStation Vita[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-112) was previously codenamed _Next Generation Portable_ (_NGP_). It was officially unveiled by Sony on January 27, 2011, at the PlayStation Meeting 2011.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-113) The original model of the handheld, the PCH-1000 series features a 5-inch OLED touchscreen,[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-114) two analog sticks, a rear touchpad, Sixaxis motion sensing and a 4 core ARM Cortex-A9 MPCore processor.

The new PCH-2000 series system is a lighter redesign of the device that was announced at the SCEJA Press Conference in September 2013 prior to the Tokyo Game Show. This model is 20% thinner and 15% lighter compared to the original model, has an additional hour of battery life, an LCD instead of OLED, includes a micro USB Type B port, and 1 GB of internal storage memory. It was released in Japan on October 10, 2013, in six colors: white, black, pink, yellow, blue, and olive green, and in North America on May 6, 2014.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-115)

The Vita was discontinued in March 2019. SIE president Jim Ryan said that while the Vita was a great device, they have moved away from portable consoles, "clearly it's a business that we're no longer in now".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-gi_first_25-13)

#### PlayStation TV

Main article: [PlayStation TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_TV "PlayStation TV")

PlayStation TV, known in Asia as PlayStation Vita TV or PS Vita TV, is a [microconsole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microconsole "Microconsole") and a non-portable variant of the PlayStation Vita handheld. It was announced on September 9, 2013, at a Sony Computer Entertainment Japan presentation. Instead of featuring a display screen, the console connects to a television via HDMI. Users can play using a Sixaxis or a DualShock 3 controller, although due to the difference in features between the controller and the handheld, certain games are not compatible with PS TV, such as those that are dependent on the system's touchscreen, rear touchpad, microphone or camera. The device is said to be compatible with over 100 Vita games, as well as various digital PlayStation Portable, PlayStation and PC Engine titles. The system supports Remote Play compatibility with the PlayStation 4, allowing players to stream games from the PS4 to a separate TV connected to PS TV, and also allows users to stream content from video services such as Hulu and Niconico, as well as access the PlayStation Store. The system was released in Japan on November 14, 2013, in North America on October 14, 2014, and in Europe and Australasia on November 14, 2014.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation#cite_note-116)

The **Xbox 360** is a [home video game console](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_video_game_console "Home video game console") developed by [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), being the successor to the [original Xbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_(console) "Xbox (console)") and the second console in the [Xbox series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox#Consoles "Xbox"). It was officially unveiled in the program titled _Xbox: The Next Generation Revealed_ on May 12, 2005, with detailed launch and game information announced later that month at the 2005 [Electronic Entertainment Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3 "E3") (E3).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-18) As a [seventh-generation console](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_generation_of_video_game_consoles "Seventh generation of video game consoles"), it primarily competed with [Sony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment")'s [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3") and Nintendo's Wii.

The Xbox 360's online service, [Xbox Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live "Xbox Live"), was expanded from its previous iteration on the original Xbox and received regular updates during the console's lifetime. Available in free and subscription-based varieties, Xbox Live allows users to [play games online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_game "Online game"); download games (through [Xbox Live Arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live_Arcade "Xbox Live Arcade")) and game demos; purchase and [stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") music, television programs, and films through the [Xbox Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Music "Xbox Music") and [Xbox Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Video "Xbox Video") portals; and access third-party content services through media streaming applications. In addition to online multimedia features, it allows users to stream media from local PCs. Several peripherals have been released, including wireless [controllers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_controller "Xbox 360 controller"), expanded [hard drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_disk_drive "Hard disk drive") storage, and the [Kinect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinect "Kinect")[motion sensing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_sensing "Motion sensing") camera. The release of these additional services and peripherals helped the Xbox brand grow from gaming-only to encompassing all multimedia, turning it into a hub for living-room computing entertainment.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-pcmag.com-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-theverge.com-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-ReferenceA-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-trlegacy-22)

[Launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_launch "Xbox 360 launch") worldwide mostly between November 2005 and December 2006, the Xbox 360 was initially in short supply in many regions, including North America and Europe. The earliest versions of the console suffered from a high [failure rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Failure_rate "Failure rate"), indicated by the so-called "[Red Ring of Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_technical_problems "Xbox 360 technical problems")", necessitating an extension of the device's warranty period. Microsoft released two redesigned models of the console: the Xbox 360 S slim model in 2010,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-360_Arcade_replacement-23) and the Xbox 360 E in 2013.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-24)

The Xbox 360 is the [tenth-highest-selling home video game console in history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_game_consoles#Home_game_consoles "List of best-selling game consoles"), and the highest-selling console made by an American company and by [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"). Although not the best-selling console of its generation, the Xbox 360 was deemed by _[TechRadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TechRadar "TechRadar")_ to be the most influential through its emphasis on digital media distribution and multiplayer gaming on Xbox Live.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-trlegacy-22)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-fool.com-25) The Xbox 360's successor, the [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"), was released on November 22, 2013.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-BBCXboxOne2013-26) On April 20, 2016, Microsoft announced that it would end the production of new Xbox 360 hardware, although the company will continue to support the platform.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-360discontinuation-7) On August 17, 2023, Microsoft announced that on July 29, 2024, the Xbox 360 game marketplace would stop offering new purchases and the Microsoft Movies & TV app will no longer function, though the console will still be able to download previously purchased content and enter multiplayer sessions, along with other online features.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-28)

## History

### Development

Known during development as Xbox Next, Xenon, Xbox 2, Xbox FS or NextBox,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Narrowing_Down_the_Xbox_Successor's_Name-29)[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving\_a\_source "Help:Archiving a source")_] the Xbox 360 was conceived in early 2003.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Development-30) In February 2003, planning for the Xenon [software platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computing_platform "Computing platform") began, and was headed by Microsoft's Vice President [J Allard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J_Allard "J Allard").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Development-30) That month, Microsoft held an event for 400 developers in [Bellevue, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellevue,_Washington "Bellevue, Washington") to recruit support for the system.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Development-30) Also that month, [Peter Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Moore_(business) "Peter Moore (business)"), former president of [Sega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sega "Sega") of America, joined Microsoft. On August 12, 2003, ATI signed on to produce the graphics processing unit for the new console, a deal that was publicly announced two days later.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-31) Before the launch of the Xbox 360, several [Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_test "Alpha test") development kits were spotted using [Apple's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.")[Power Mac G5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_Mac_G5 "Power Mac G5") hardware. This was because the system's [PowerPC 970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerPC_970 "PowerPC 970") processor was running the same [PowerPC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerPC "PowerPC") architecture that the Xbox 360 would eventually run under [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM")'s [Xenon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenon_(processor) "Xenon (processor)") processor. The cores of the Xenon [processor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_processing_unit "Central processing unit") were developed using a slightly modified version of the [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3")'s [Cell Processor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(microprocessor) "Cell (microprocessor)") PPE architecture. According to David Shippy and Mickie Phipps, the IBM employees were "hiding" their work from Sony and Toshiba, IBM's partners in developing the Cell Processor.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-32)[Jeff Minter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Minter "Jeff Minter") created the [music visualization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_visualization "Music visualization") program [Neon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neon_(light_synthesizer) "Neon (light synthesizer)") which is included with the Xbox 360.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-33)

### Launch

Main article: [Xbox 360 launch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_launch "Xbox 360 launch")

The Xbox 360 was released on November 22, 2005, in the United States and Canada;[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-nalaunch-3) December 2, 2005, in Europe and December 10, 2005, in Japan. It was later launched in Mexico, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, India, and Russia. In its first year in the market, the system was launched in 36 countries, more countries than any other console has launched in a single year.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-34)

### Critical reception

In 2009, _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ named the Xbox 360 the sixth-greatest video game console of all time, out of a field of 25.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-35) Although not the best-selling console of the seventh generation, the Xbox 360 was deemed by _[TechRadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TechRadar "TechRadar")_ to be the most influential, by emphasizing digital media distribution and online gaming through Xbox Live, and by popularizing [game achievement awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achievement_(video_games) "Achievement (video games)").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-trlegacy-22)_PC Magazine_ considered the Xbox 360 the prototype for online gaming as it "proved that online gaming communities could thrive in the console space".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-pcmag.com-19) Five years after the Xbox 360's debut, the well-received [Kinect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinect "Kinect") motion capture camera was released, which set the record of being the fastest selling consumer electronic device in history, and extended the life of the console.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-finance.yahoo.com-36)_[Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge\_(magazine) "Edge (magazine)")_ ranked Xbox 360 the second-best console of the 1993–2013 period, stating "It had its own social network, cross-game chat, new indie games every week, and the best version of just about every multiformat game... _[Killzone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killzone\_(series) "Killzone (series)")_ is no _[Halo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halo\_(series) "Halo (series)")_ and nowadays _[Gran Turismo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran\_Turismo\_(series) "Gran Turismo (series)")_ is no _[Forza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forza\_Motorsport\_(series) "Forza Motorsport (series)")_, but it's not about the exclusives—there's nothing to trump [Naughty Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naughty_Dog "Naughty Dog")'s PS3 output, after all. Rather, it's about the choices Microsoft made back in the original Xbox's lifetime. The PC-like architecture meant the early EA Sports games ran at 60fps compared to only 30 on PS3, Xbox Live meant every dedicated player had an existing friends list, and _Halo_ meant Microsoft had the killer next-generation exclusive. And when developers demo games on PC now they do it with a 360 pad—another industry benchmark, and a critical one."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-37)
