The Xbox 360 began production only 69 days before launch, on September 14, 2005,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-bottleneck-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-46) and Microsoft was not able to supply enough systems to meet initial consumer demand in Europe or North America, selling out completely [upon release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_launch "Xbox 360 launch") in all regions except in Japan.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Shortages_spoil_Xbox_360_launch-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Xbox_360_Launch_Takes_Europe_by_Storm-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Retailers_Sell_Out_of_Initial_Xbox_360_Shipments-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-bbc-soldout-50) Forty thousand units were offered for sale on auction site [eBay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EBay "EBay") during the initial week of release, 10% of the total supply.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-51) By year's end, Microsoft had shipped 1.5 million units, including 900,000 in North America, 500,000 in Europe, and 100,000 in Japan.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-52)

In May 2008, Microsoft announced that 10 million Xbox 360s had been sold and that it was the "first current generation gaming console" to surpass the 10 million figure in the US.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-53) In the US, the Xbox 360 was the leader in current-generation home console sales until June 2008, when it was surpassed by the Wii.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-56) By the end of March 2011, Xbox 360 sales in the US had reached 25.4 million units.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-EMEA,_US=25.4mil-40) Between January 2011 and October 2013, the Xbox 360 was the best-selling console in the United States for these 32 consecutive months.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-57) By the end of 2014, Xbox 360 sales had surpassed sales of the Wii, making the Xbox 360 the best-selling 7th-generation console in the US once again.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-58) In Canada, the Xbox 360 has sold a total of 870,000 units as of August 1, 2008.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-canadianpress-59) According to data from [Circana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circana "Circana"), lifetime Xbox 360 sales in the United States reached 42.7 million units.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-MatPiscatella_lifetime_US_sales_bsky-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-VGChartz_US_lifetime_sales-39)

In Europe, the Xbox 360 has sold seven million units as of November 20, 2008.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Europesales-60) The Xbox 360 took 110 weeks to reach 2 million units sold in the UK, generating £507m in revenue.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-360_9mUKGamesIndustry.biz-41) Sales in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") would reach 3.2 million units by January 2009, per [GfK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GfK "GfK")[Chart-Track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chart-Track "Chart-Track").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-61) The 8 million unit mark was crossed in the UK by February 2013.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-62) Sales of the Xbox 360 would overtake the Wii later that year, topping 9 million units, making the Xbox 360 the best-selling 7th-generation console in the UK, as well as making it the third best-selling console of all time in the region, behind the PS2 and Nintendo DS.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-63)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-360_9mUKGamesIndustry.biz-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-ChrisDringtweetGamesIndustry.biz-42) Over 1 million units were sold in [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain") across the console's lifecycle.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-64)

The Xbox 360 crossed the 1 million units sold in Japan in March 2009,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-65) and the 1.5 million units sold in June 2011.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-66) Lifetime sales of the Xbox 360 in Japan stand at 1,616,218 million units. While the Xbox 360 has sold poorly in Japan, it improved upon the sales of the original [Xbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_(console) "Xbox (console)"), which had total sales of 474,992 units.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-XboxJPsales-43) Furthermore, the Xbox 360 managed to outsell both the PlayStation 3 and Wii the week ending September 14, 2008, as well as the week ending February 22, 2009, when the Japanese Xbox 360 exclusives _[Infinite Undiscovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinite\_Undiscovery "Infinite Undiscovery")_[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-67) and _[Star Ocean: The Last Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Ocean:\_The\_Last\_Hope "Star Ocean: The Last Hope")_,[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-68) were released those weeks, respectively. Ultimately, _[Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge\_(magazine) "Edge (magazine)")_ magazine would report that Microsoft had been unable to make serious inroads into the dominance of domestic rivals Sony and Nintendo; adding that lackluster sales in Japan had led to retailers scaling down and in some cases, discontinuing sales of the Xbox 360 completely.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-69) The significance of Japan's poor sales might be overstated in the media in comparison to overall international sales.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-3_October_2014-70)

### Legacy

The Xbox 360 sold much better than its predecessor, and although not the best-selling console of the seventh generation, it is regarded as a success since it strengthened Microsoft as a major force in the console market at the expense of well-established rivals.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-fool.com-25) The inexpensive Wii did sell the most console units but eventually saw a collapse of third-party software support in its later years, and it has been viewed by some as a fad since the succeeding [Wii U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U "Wii U") had a poor debut in 2012.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-trlegacy-22)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-theglobeandmail-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-74) The [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3") struggled for a time due to being too expensive and initially lacking quality games,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-75) making it far less dominant than its predecessor, the PlayStation 2, and it took until late in the PlayStation 3's lifespan for its sales and games to reach parity with the Xbox 360. _TechRadar_ proclaimed that "Xbox 360 passes the baton as the king of the hill – a position that puts all the more pressure on its successor, Xbox One".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-trlegacy-22)

The Xbox 360's advantage over its competitors was due to the release of high-profile games from both first party and third-party developers. The 2007 [Game Critics Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Critics_Awards "Game Critics Awards") honored the platform with 38 nominations and 12 wins – more than any other platform.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-77) By March 2008, the Xbox 360 had reached a software [attach rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attach_rate "Attach rate") of 7.5 games per console in the US; the rate was 7.0 in Europe, while its competitors were 3.8 (PS3) and 3.5 (Wii), according to Microsoft.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-78) At the 2008 [Game Developers Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developers_Conference "Game Developers Conference"), Microsoft announced that it expected over 1,000 games available for Xbox 360 by the end of the year.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-79) As well as enjoying exclusives such as additions to the Halo franchise and _[Gears of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gears\_of\_War "Gears of War")_, the Xbox 360 has managed to gain a simultaneous release of games that were initially planned to be PS3 exclusives, including _[Devil May Cry 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devil\_May\_Cry\_4 "Devil May Cry 4")_,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Devil_May_Cry-80)_[Ace Combat 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace\_Combat\_6 "Ace Combat 6")_,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Ace_Combat-81)_[Virtua Fighter 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtua\_Fighter\_5 "Virtua Fighter 5")_,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Virtua_Fighter-82)_[Grand Theft Auto IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto\_IV "Grand Theft Auto IV")_,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Grand_Theft_Auto_4-83)_[Final Fantasy XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final\_Fantasy\_XIII "Final Fantasy XIII")_,[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-FFXIII360-84)_[Tekken 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tekken\_6 "Tekken 6")_,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-tekken360-85)_[Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal\_Gear\_Rising:\_Revengeance "Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance")_,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-86) and _[L.A. Noire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A.\_Noire "L.A. Noire")_.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-87) In addition, Xbox 360 versions of cross-platform games were generally considered superior to their PS3 counterparts in 2006 and 2007, due in part to the difficulties of programming for the PS3.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-88)

_[TechRadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TechRadar "TechRadar")_ deemed the Xbox 360 as the most influential game system through its emphasis of digital media distribution, Xbox Live online gaming service, and [game achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achievement_(video_games) "Achievement (video games)") feature.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-trlegacy-22) During the console's lifetime, the Xbox brand has grown from gaming-only to encompassing all multimedia, turning it into a hub for "living-room computing environment".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-businessweek.com-89)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-theverge.com-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-ReferenceA-21)

Microsoft announced the successor to the Xbox 360, the [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"), on May 21, 2013.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-BBCXboxOne2013-26) On April 20, 2016, Microsoft announced the end of production of new Xbox 360 hardware, though the company will continue to provide hardware and software support for the platform as selected Xbox 360 games are playable on Xbox One.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-verge-360endofproduction-90) The Xbox 360 maintained an unusually long commercial lifespan, receiving continued software support from major publishers and new title releases as late as 2018, nearly five years after the launch of its successor, the Xbox One.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-91) The Xbox 360 continues to have an active player base years after the system's discontinuation. Speaking to _[Engadget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engadget "Engadget")_ at [E3 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2019 "E3 2019") after the announcement of [Project Scarlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_Series_S "Xbox Series X and Series S"), the next-generation of Xbox consoles after the Xbox One, [Phil Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Spencer_(Microsoft) "Phil Spencer (Microsoft)") stated that there were still "millions and millions of players" active on the Xbox 360.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-92) After the launch of the [Xbox Series X and S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_S "Xbox Series X and S") by the end of 2020, the Xbox 360 still had a 17.7% market share of all consoles in use in Mexico; comparatively, newer systems like the Xbox One and [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") stood at 36.9% and 18.0% market share, respectively.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-93)

## Hardware

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Microsoft-Xbox-360-E-wController.jpg/250px-Microsoft-Xbox-360-E-wController.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Microsoft-Xbox-360-E-wController.jpg)

The Xbox 360 E model, announced at [E3 2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2013 "E3 2013"), shares many aesthetics with the [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One").

The main unit of the Xbox 360 itself has slight double concavity in matte white or black. The official color of the white model is Arctic Chill. It features a port on the top when vertical (left side when horizontal) to which a custom-housed [hard disk drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_disk_drive "Hard disk drive") unit can be attached.

On the Slim and E models, the hard drive bay is on the bottom when vertical (right side when horizontal) and requires the opening of a concealed door to access it. (This does not void the warranty.) The Xbox 360 Slim/E [hard drives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_disk_drive "Hard disk drive") are standard 2.5" [SATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_ATA "Serial ATA") laptop drives,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-94) but have a custom enclosure and firmware so that the Xbox 360 can recognize it.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-95)

### Technical specifications

Main article: [Xbox 360 technical specifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_technical_specifications "Xbox 360 technical specifications")

The Xbox 360 uses the triple-core [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM") designed [Xenon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenon_(processor) "Xenon (processor)") as its CPU, with each core capable of simultaneously processing two [threads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thread_(computer_science) "Thread (computer science)"), and can therefore operate on up to six threads at once.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-96)[Graphics processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_graphics "Computer graphics") is handled by the [ATI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATI_Technologies "ATI Technologies")[Xenos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenos_(graphics_chip) "Xenos (graphics chip)"), which has 10[MB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megabyte "Megabyte") of [eDRAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EDRAM "EDRAM"). Its main memory pool is 512 MB in size.

Originally, the Xbox 360 was equipped with only 256 MB of RAM, but [Epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Games "Epic Games"), the [_Gears of War_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gears_of_War_(video_game) "Gears of War (video game)") developer, demonstrated to Microsoft that the console should have 512 MB of RAM to deliver much better performance. When asked about this, Epic Games Executive Vice President Mark Rein said in 2006: "So the day they made the decision, we were apparently the first developer they called; we were at Game Developers Conference, was it two years ago, and then I got a call from the chief financial officer of MGS and he said 'I just want you to know you cost me a billion dollars' and I said, 'we did a favour for a billion gamers'."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-97)

Various hard disk drives have been produced, including options at 20, 60, 120, 250, 320, or 500 GB.

Main article: [Kinect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinect "Kinect")

It was first announced on June 1, 2009, at the [Electronic Entertainment Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Entertainment_Expo "Electronic Entertainment Expo"), under the codename, _Project Natal_.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-102) The add-on [peripheral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral "Peripheral") enables users to control and interact with the Xbox 360 without a [game controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_controller "Game controller") by using gestures, [spoken commands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_recognition "Speech recognition") and presented objects and images. The Kinect accessory is compatible with all Xbox 360 models,[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-103) connecting to new models via a custom connector, and to older ones via a USB and mains power adapter.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-104) During their [CES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_Electronics_Show "Consumer Electronics Show") 2010 keynote speech, Robbie Bach and Microsoft CEO [Steve Ballmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ballmer "Steve Ballmer") went on to say that Kinect would be released during the holiday period (November–January) and work with every Xbox 360 console. ### Technical problems

Main article: [Xbox 360 technical problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_technical_problems "Xbox 360 technical problems")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Xbox360-ringofdeath.jpg/250px-Xbox360-ringofdeath.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Xbox360-ringofdeath.jpg)

Three red lights on the Xbox 360's ring indicator representing a "General Error requiring service of the Console or Power Adapter", commonly nicknamed the "Red Ring of Death"

The original model of the Xbox 360 has been subject to a number of [technical problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_technical_problems "Xbox 360 technical problems"). Since the console's release in 2005, users have reported concerns over its reliability and [failure rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Failure_rate "Failure rate").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-120)

To aid customers with defective consoles, Microsoft extended the Xbox 360's manufacturer's warranty to three years for hardware failure problems that generate a "General Hardware Failure" error report. A "General Hardware Failure" is recognized on all models released before the Xbox 360 S by three quadrants of the ring around the power button flashing red. This error is often known as the "[Red Ring of Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Ring_of_Death "Red Ring of Death")".[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-121) In April 2009, the warranty was extended to also cover failures related to the E74 [error code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Error_code "Error code").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-122) The warranty extension is not granted for any other types of failures that do not generate these specific error codes.

After these problems surfaced, Microsoft attempted to modify the console to improve its reliability. Modifications included a reduction in the number, size, and placement of components, the addition of dabs of epoxy on the corners and edges of the CPU and GPU as glue to prevent movement relative to the board during heat expansion,[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-123) and a second GPU heatsink to dissipate more heat.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-repaired_hardware-124) With the release of the redesigned Xbox 360 S, the warranty for the newer models does not include the three-year extended coverage for "General Hardware Failures".[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-125) The newer Xbox 360 S and E models indicate system overheating when the console's power button begins to flash red, unlike previous models where the first and third quadrant of the ring would light up red around the power button if overheating occurred. The system will then warn the user of imminent system shutdown until the system has cooled,[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-126) whereas a flashing power button that alternates between green and red is an indication of a "General Hardware Failure" unlike older models where three of the quadrants would light up red.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-127) Motherboards primarily suffering from the red ring of death are Xenon, Zephyr, and earlier Falcons. [[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-128)

Mistwalker's first game, _[Blue Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Dragon\_(video\_game) "Blue Dragon (video game)")_, was released in 2006 and had a limited-edition bundle which sold out quickly with over 10,000 pre-orders.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Blue_Dragon_PreOrders-139)_Blue Dragon_ is one of three Xbox 360 games to surpass 200,000 units in Japan, along with _[Tales of Vesperia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tales\_of\_Vesperia "Tales of Vesperia")_ and _[Star Ocean: The Last Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Ocean:\_The\_Last\_Hope "Star Ocean: The Last Hope")_. By 2015, game releases started to decline as most publishers instead focused on the [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"). As one of the late updates to the software following its discontinuation, Microsoft will add the ability for Xbox 360 users to use cloud saves even if they do not have Xbox Live Gold prior to the launch of the [Xbox Series X and Series S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_Series_S "Xbox Series X and Series S") in November 2020. The new consoles will have backward compatibility for all Xbox 360 games that are already backward compatible on the Xbox One and can use any Xbox 360 game's cloud saves through this update, making the transition to the new consoles easier.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-142)

### Interface

Main article: [Xbox 360 system software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_system_software "Xbox 360 system software")

The Xbox 360's original [graphical user interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphical_user_interface "Graphical user interface") was the _Xbox 360 Dashboard_; a [tabbed interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tab_(GUI) "Tab (GUI)") that featured five "Blades" (formerly four blades), and was designed by [AKQA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AKQA "AKQA")[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-143) and [Audiobrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiobrain "Audiobrain"). It could be launched automatically when the console [booted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booting "Booting") without a disc in it, or when the disc tray was ejected, but the user had the option to select what the console does if a game is in the tray on start up, or if inserted when already on. A simplified version of it was also accessible at any time via the Xbox Guide button on the gamepad.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-144) This simplified version showed the user's gamercard, Xbox Live messages and friends list. It also allowed for personal and music settings, in addition to voice or video chats, or returning to the Xbox Dashboard from the game.

On November 19, 2008, the Xbox 360's dashboard was changed from the "Blade" interface to a dashboard reminiscent of that present on the Zune and Windows Media Center, known as the "New Xbox Experience" or NXE.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-145)

Since the console's release, Microsoft has released several updates for the Dashboard software.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-146)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-147) These updates have included adding new features to the console, enhancing Xbox Live functionality and multimedia playback capabilities, adding compatibility for new accessories, and fixing bugs in the software. Such updates are mandatory for users wishing to use Xbox Live, as access to Xbox Live is disabled until the update is performed.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

#### New Xbox Experience

Further information: [Xbox 360 system software §User interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360_system_software#User_interface "Xbox 360 system software")

At E3 2008, at Microsoft's Show, Microsoft's Aaron Greenberg and Marc Whitten announced the new Xbox 360 interface called the "New Xbox Experience" (NXE). The update was intended to ease console menu navigation. Its GUI uses the Twist UI, previously used in [Windows Media Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Media_Center "Windows Media Center") and the [Zune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zune "Zune"). Its new Xbox Guide retains all Dashboard functionality (including the Marketplace browser and disk ejection) and the original "Blade" interface (although the color scheme has been changed to match that of the NXE Dashboard).[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-148)

The NXE also provides many new features. Users can now install games from disc to the hard drive to play them with reduced load time and less disc drive noise, but each game's disc must remain in the system in order to run. A new, built-in Community system allows the creation of digitized [Avatars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(Xbox_360) "Avatar (Xbox 360)") that can be used for multiple activities, such as sharing photos or playing [Arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live_Arcade "Xbox Live Arcade") games like _[1 vs. 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1\_vs\_100\_(Xbox\_360) "1 vs 100 (Xbox 360)")_. The update was released on November 19, 2008.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-xbox2-149)

While previous system updates have been stored on internal memory, the NXE update was the first to require a storage device—at least a 128 MB memory card or a [hard drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_disk_drive "Hard disk drive").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-150)

Microsoft released a further update to the Xbox 360 Dashboard starting on December 6, 2011.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-151) It included a completely new user interface which utilizes Microsoft's [Metro design language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_(design_language) "Metro (design language)") and added new features such as cloud storage for game saves and profiles, live television, [Bing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Bing "Microsoft Bing") voice search,[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-152) access to YouTube videos and better support for Kinect voice commands.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-153)

### Multimedia

The Xbox 360 supports videos in [Windows Media Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Media_Video "Windows Media Video") (WMV) format (including [high-definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_television "High-definition television") and [PlaysForSure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_PlaysForSure "Microsoft PlaysForSure") videos), as well as [H.264](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.264/MPEG-4_AVC "H.264/MPEG-4 AVC") and [MPEG-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPEG-4 "MPEG-4") media. The December 2007 dashboard update added support for the playback of [MPEG-4 ASP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPEG-4_Part_2 "MPEG-4 Part 2") format videos.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-154) The console can also [display pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(computing) "Avatar (computing)") and perform slideshows of photo collections with various transition effects, and supports audio playback, with [music player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_audio_player "Digital audio player") controls accessible through the Xbox 360 Guide button. Users may play back their own music while playing games or using the dashboard and can play music with an interactive visual synthesizer.

Music, photos and videos can be played from standard USB [mass storage devices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_storage_device "Data storage device"), Xbox 360 proprietary [storage devices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_storage_device "Data storage device") (such as memory cards or Xbox 360 hard drives), and servers or computers with [Windows Media Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Media_Center "Windows Media Center") or [Windows XP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_XP "Windows XP") with [Service pack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_pack "Service pack") 2 or higher within the local-area network in streaming mode.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-155)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-156) As the Xbox 360 uses a modified version of the [UPnP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Plug_and_Play "Universal Plug and Play") AV protocol,[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-157)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] some alternative UPnP servers such as uShare (part of the [GeeXboX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeeXboX "GeeXboX") project) and [MythTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MythTV "MythTV") can also stream media to the Xbox 360, allowing for similar functionality from non-Windows servers. This is possible with video files up to HD-resolution and with several [codecs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codec "Codec") (MPEG-2, MPEG-4, WMV) and [container formats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Container_format_(digital) "Container format (digital)") (WMV, MOV, TS).[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-158)

As of October 27, 2009,[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-159) UK and Ireland users are also able to access live and on-demand streams of [Sky television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_Digital_(UK_&_Ireland) "Sky Digital (UK & Ireland)") programming.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-160)

At the 2007, 2008, and 2009 [Consumer Electronics Shows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_Electronics_Show "Consumer Electronics Show"), Microsoft had announced that [IPTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPTV "IPTV") services would soon be made available to use through the Xbox 360. In 2007, Microsoft chairman [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") stated that IPTV on Xbox 360 was expected to be available to consumers by the holiday season, using the [Microsoft TV IPTV Edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_TV_IPTV_Edition "Microsoft TV IPTV Edition") platform.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-161) In 2008, Gates and president of Entertainment & Devices [Robbie Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_J._Bach "Robert J. Bach") announced a partnership with [BT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_Retail "BT Retail") in the United Kingdom, in which the [BT Vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BT_Vision "BT Vision") advanced TV service, using the newer [Microsoft Mediaroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Mediaroom "Microsoft Mediaroom") IPTV platform, would be accessible via Xbox 360, planned for the middle of the year.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-162) BT Vision's DVR-based features would not be available on Xbox 360 due to limited hard drive capacity.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-163) In 2010, while announcing version 2.0 of Microsoft Mediaroom, Microsoft CEO [Steve Ballmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ballmer "Steve Ballmer") mentioned that AT&T's [U-verse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U-verse "U-verse") IPTV service would enable Xbox 360s to be used as set-top boxes later in the year.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-164) As of January 2010, IPTV on Xbox 360 has yet to be deployed beyond limited trials.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2012, Microsoft released the Live Event Player, allowing for events such as video game shows, beauty pageants, award shows, concerts, news and sporting events to be streamed on the console via Xbox Live. The first live events streamed on Live were the 2012 [Revolver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolver_(magazine) "Revolver (magazine)") Golden Gods, Microsoft's [E3 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2012 "E3 2012") media briefing and the [Miss Teen USA 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Teen_USA_2012 "Miss Teen USA 2012") beauty pageant.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### XNA community

Main article: [Microsoft XNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_XNA "Microsoft XNA")

XNA Community is a feature whereby Xbox 360 owners can receive community-created games, made with Microsoft XNA Game Studio, from the XNA Creators Club. The games are written, published, and distributed through a community managed portal. XNA Community provides a channel for digital videogame delivery over Xbox Live that can be free of royalties, publishers and licenses.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-166) XNA game sales, however, did not meet original expectations,[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-167) though [Xbox Live Indie Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live_Indie_Games "Xbox Live Indie Games") (XBLIG) has had some "hits".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Services

### Xbox Live

Main article: [Xbox Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live "Xbox Live")

When the Xbox 360 was released, Microsoft's online gaming service Xbox Live was shut down for 24 hours and underwent a major upgrade, adding a basic non-subscription service called Xbox Live Silver (later renamed Xbox Live Free) to its already established premium subscription-based service (which was renamed Gold). Xbox Live Free is included with all [SKUs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock-keeping_unit "Stock-keeping unit") of the console. It allows users to create a user profile, join on [message boards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_forum "Internet forum"), and access Microsoft's Xbox Live Arcade and Marketplace and talk to other members.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-XboxLiveFree-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-169) A Live Free account does not generally support multiplayer gaming; however, some games that have rather limited online functions already (such as _[Viva Piñata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viva\_Pi%C3%B1ata "Viva Piñata")_) and games that feature their own subscription service (e.g. [EA Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports "EA Sports") games) can be played with a Free account. Xbox Live also supports voice, a feature possible with the Xbox Live Vision.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-170)

Xbox Live Gold includes the same features as Free and includes integrated [online game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_game "Online game") playing capabilities outside of third-party subscriptions. Microsoft has allowed previous Xbox Live subscribers to maintain their profile information, [friends list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contact_list "Contact list"), and games history when they make the transition to Xbox Live Gold. To transfer an Xbox Live account to the new system, users need to link a [Windows Live ID](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Live_ID "Windows Live ID") to their gamertag on Xbox.com.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-171) When users add an Xbox Live enabled profile to their console, they are required to provide the console with their passport account information and the last four digits of their [credit card number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_card_number "Payment card number"), which is used for verification purposes and billing. An Xbox Live Gold account has an annual cost of US$59.99, [C$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_dollar "Canadian dollar")59.99, [NZ$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_dollar "New Zealand dollar")90.00, [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")39.99, or €59.99. On January 5, 2011, Xbox Live reached over 30 million subscribers.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-172)

### Xbox Live Marketplace

Main article: [Xbox Live Marketplace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live_Marketplace "Xbox Live Marketplace")

The Xbox Live Marketplace was a virtual market designed for the console that allows Xbox Live users to download purchased or promotional content. The service offers movie and game trailers, [game demos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_demo "Game demo"), Xbox Live Arcade games and Xbox 360 Dashboard themes as well as add-on game content (items, costumes, levels etc.). These features are available to both Free and Gold members on Xbox Live. A hard drive or memory unit is required to store products purchased from Xbox Live Marketplace.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-173) In order to download priced content, users are required to purchase [Microsoft Points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Points "Microsoft Points") for use as [scrip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scrip "Scrip");[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-174) though some products (such as trailers and demos) are free to download. Microsoft Points can be obtained through prepaid cards in 1,600 and 4,000-point denominations. Microsoft Points can also be purchased through Xbox Live with a credit card in 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 5,000-point denominations. Users are able to view items available to download on the service through a PC via the [Xbox Live Marketplace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live_Marketplace "Xbox Live Marketplace") website.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-175) An estimated 70 percent of Xbox Live users have downloaded items from the Marketplace.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Live_Stats-176) The Xbox 360 Marketplace was discontinued on July 29, 2024.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-177)

### Xbox Live Arcade

Main article: [Xbox Live Arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live_Arcade "Xbox Live Arcade")

Xbox Live Arcade is an online service operated by Microsoft that is used to distribute downloadable video games to Xbox and Xbox 360 owners. In addition to classic [arcade games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_game "Arcade game") such as _[Ms. Pac-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ms.\_Pac-Man "Ms. Pac-Man")_, the service offers some new original games like _[Assault Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assault\_Heroes "Assault Heroes")_. The Xbox Live Arcade also features games from other consoles, such as the PlayStation game _[Castlevania: Symphony of the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castlevania:\_Symphony\_of\_the\_Night "Castlevania: Symphony of the Night")_ and [PC games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer_game "Personal computer game") such as _[Zuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuma\_(video\_game) "Zuma (video game)")_. The service was first launched on November 3, 2004,[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-178) using a DVD to load, and offered games for about US$5 to $15. Items are purchased using Microsoft Points, a proprietary currency used to reduce credit card transaction charges. On November 22, 2005, Xbox Live Arcade was re-launched with the release of the Xbox 360, in which it was now integrated with the Xbox 360's dashboard. The games are generally aimed toward more casual gamers; examples of the more popular games are _[Geometry Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometry\_Wars "Geometry Wars")_, _[Street Fighter II' Hyper Fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street\_Fighter\_II\_Turbo:\_Hyper\_Fighting "Street Fighter II Turbo: Hyper Fighting")_, and _[Uno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uno\_(video\_game) "Uno (video game)")_.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-179) On March 24, 2010, Microsoft introduced the [Game Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Room "Game Room") to Xbox Live. Game Room is a gaming service for Xbox 360 and Microsoft Windows that lets players compete in classic arcade and console games in a virtual arcade.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-180)

### Movies and TV

Main article: [Microsoft Movies & TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Movies_&_TV "Microsoft Movies & TV")

On November 6, 2006, Microsoft announced the Xbox Video Marketplace, an exclusive video store accessible through the console. Launched in the United States on November 22, 2006, the first anniversary of the Xbox 360's launch, the service allows users in the United States to download high-definition and standard-definition television shows and movies onto an Xbox 360 console for viewing. With the exception of short clips, content is not currently[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] available for streaming, and must be downloaded. Movies are also available for rental. They expire in 14 days after download or at the end of the first 24 hours after the movie has begun playing, whichever comes first. Television episodes can be purchased to own, and are transferable to an unlimited number of consoles. Downloaded files use 5.1 [surround audio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surround_sound "Surround sound") and are encoded using [VC-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VC-1 "VC-1") for video at 720p, with a [bitrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bit_rate "Bit rate") of 6.8 Mbit/s.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Xbox_360_live_video-181) Television content is offered from MTV, [VH1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VH1 "VH1"), [Comedy Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Central "Comedy Central"), [Turner Broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turner_Broadcasting_System "Turner Broadcasting System"), and [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS"); and movie content is [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros."), [Paramount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures"), and [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company"), along with other publishers.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Live_Video_announcement-182)

After the Spring 2007 update, the following [video codecs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_codec "Video codec") are supported:

*   H.264 video support: Up to 15 Mbit/s, Baseline, Main, and High (up to level 4.1) Profiles with [2 channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2channel "2channel") AAC LC and Main Profiles.
*   MPEG-4 Part 2 video support: Up to 8 Mbit/s, Simple Profile with 2 channel AAC LC and Main Profiles.

As a late addition to the December Xbox 360 update, 25 movies were added to the European Xbox 360 video market place on the December 11, 2007 and cost 250 Microsoft points for the SD version of the movie and 380 points for the HD version of the movie.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Video_Marketplace_launches_in_Europe-183) Xbox Live members in Canada featured the ability to go on the Xbox Live Marketplace also as of December 11, 2007 with around 30 movies to be downloaded for the same number of Microsoft Points.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-184)

On May 26, 2009, Microsoft announced it would release the [Zune HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zune_HD "Zune HD") (in the fall of 2009), which was then the next addition to the [Zune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zune "Zune") product range. This was of an impact on the Xbox Live Video Store as it was also announced that the Zune Video Marketplace and the Xbox Live Video Store will be merged to form the [Zune Marketplace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zune_Marketplace "Zune Marketplace"), which will be arriving on Xbox Live in 7 countries initially, the United Kingdom, the United States, France, Italy, Germany, Ireland and Spain.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-Zune_Marketplace-185) Further details were released at the Microsoft press conference at [E3 2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2009 "E3 2009").[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-186)

On October 16, 2012, Xbox Video and Xbox Music were released, replacing the Zune Marketplace. Xbox Video is a digital video service on that offers full HD movies and TV series for purchase or rental on Xbox 360, Windows 8, [Windows RT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_RT "Windows RT") PCs and [tablets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tablet_computer "Tablet computer"), and Windows Phones.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-187)

On August 18, 2015, Microsoft rolled out an update renaming it Movies and TV similar to the Windows 10 App.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-188)

### Groove Music

Main article: [Groove Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groove_Music "Groove Music")

[Xbox Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Music "Xbox Music") provides 30 million music tracks available for purchase or access through subscription. It was announced at the [Electronic Entertainment Expo 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Entertainment_Expo_2012 "Electronic Entertainment Expo 2012") and it integrates with [Windows 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_8 "Windows 8") and [Windows Phone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Phone "Windows Phone") as well.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-189)

In August 2015 Microsoft rolled out an update renaming it to Groove Music similar to the Windows 10 App.

### Xbox SmartGlass

Main article: [Xbox SmartGlass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_SmartGlass "Xbox SmartGlass")

Xbox SmartGlass allows for integration between the Xbox 360 console and mobile devices such as tablets and smartphones.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-190) An app is available on Android, Windows Phone 8 and iOS. Users of the feature can view additional content to accompany the game they are playing, or the TV shows and movies they are watching. They can also use their mobile device as a remote to control the Xbox 360.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-191) The SmartGlass functionality can also be found in the Xbox 360's successor, the [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One").

## Game development

PartnerNet, the developers-only alternative [Xbox Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live "Xbox Live") network used by developers to beta test game content developed for [Xbox Live Arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Live_Arcade "Xbox Live Arcade"),[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-192) runs on Xbox 360 [debug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debugging "Debugging") kits, which are used both by developers and by the gaming press. In a podcast released on February 12, 2007, a developer breached the PartnerNet [non-disclosure agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-disclosure_agreement "Non-disclosure agreement") (NDA) by commenting that he had found a playable version of _[Alien Hominid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alien\_Hominid "Alien Hominid")_ and an unplayable version of _[Ikaruga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ikaruga "Ikaruga")_ on PartnerNet. A few video game journalists, misconstruing the breach of the NDA as an invalidation of the NDA, immediately began reporting on other games being tested via PartnerNet, including a remake of _[Jetpac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jetpac "Jetpac")_.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-193) (_Alien Hominid_ for the Xbox 360 was released on February 28 of that year, and _Ikaruga_ was released over a year later on April 9, 2008. _Jetpac_ was released for the Xbox 360 on March 28, 2007, as _[Jetpac Refuelled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jetpac\_Refuelled "Jetpac Refuelled")_). There have also been numerous video and screenshot leaks of game footage on PartnerNet, as well as a complete version of _[Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonic\_the\_Hedgehog\_4:\_Episode\_I "Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode I")_, which caused for the whole PartnerNet service to be shut down overnight on April 3, 2010.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-194) In the following days, [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") reminded developers and journalists that they were in breach of NDA by sharing information about PartnerNet content and asked websites to remove lists of games in development that were discovered on the service.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-195) Sega used feedback from fans about the leaked version of Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode I to refine it before they eventually released it.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-196) Additionally, a pair of hackers played their modded Halo 3 games on PartnerNet in addition to using PartnerNet to find unreleased and untested software. The hackers passed this information along to their friends before they were eventually caught by Bungie. Consequently, Bungie left a message for the hackers on PartnerNet which read "Winners Don't Break Into PartnerNet".[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-197) Other games that were leaked in the PartnerNet fiasco include [Shenmue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenmue_(video_game) "Shenmue (video game)") and [Shenmue II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenmue_II "Shenmue II").[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360#cite_note-198)

The **PlayStation Portable**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-6) (**PSP**) is a [handheld game console](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handheld_game_console "Handheld game console") developed and marketed by [Sony Computer Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment"). It was first released in Japan on December 12, 2004, in North America on March 24, 2005, and in [PAL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PAL "PAL") regions on September 1, 2005, and is the first handheld installment in the PlayStation line of consoles. As a [seventh generation console](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_generation_of_video_game_consoles "Seventh generation of video game consoles"), the PSP competed with the Nintendo DS.

Development of the PSP was announced during [E3 2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2003 "E3 2003"), and the console was unveiled at a Sony press conference on May 11, 2004. The system was the most powerful portable console at the time of its introduction, and was the first viable competitor to Nintendo's handheld consoles after many challengers such as [Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia "Nokia")'s [N-Gage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-Gage_(device) "N-Gage (device)") had failed. The PSP's advanced graphics capabilities made it a popular mobile entertainment device, which could connect to the PlayStation 2 and [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3"), any computer with a USB interface, other PSP systems, and the [Internet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet "Internet"). The PSP also had a vast array of multimedia features such as video playback and audio playback, leading some to classify it as a [portable media player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portable_media_player "Portable media player") as well.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-8) The PSP is the only handheld console to use an optical disc format—in this case, [Universal Media Disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Media_Disc "Universal Media Disc") (UMD)—as its primary storage medium; both games and movies were released on the format.

The PSP was received positively by critics, and sold over 80 million units during its ten-year lifetime. Several models of the console were released, including the PSP Street and the PSP Go. The PSP line was succeeded by the [PlayStation Vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Vita "PlayStation Vita"), released in Japan in December 2011 and worldwide in February 2012. The Vita has [backward compatibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backward_compatibility "Backward compatibility") with PSP games that were released on the [PlayStation Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Network "PlayStation Network") through the [PlayStation Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Store "PlayStation Store"), which became the main method of purchasing PSP games until Sony shut down access to the store from the PSP on March 31, 2016. Hardware shipments of the PSP ended worldwide in 2014;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-9) production of UMDs ended when the last Japanese factory producing them closed in late 2016.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Sony Computer Entertainment first announced development of the PlayStation Portable at a press conference preceding [E3 2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2003 "E3 2003").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-EuroE32003-10) Although samples were not presented,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-EuroE32003-10) Sony released extensive technical details.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-11) CEO Ken Kutaragi called the device the "[Walkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkman "Walkman") of the 21st century", a reference to the console's multimedia capabilities.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-12) Several gaming websites were impressed with the handheld's computing capabilities, and looked forward to its potential as a gaming platform.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-IGNE32003-13)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-EuroE32003-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-14)

In the 1990s, Nintendo had dominated the handheld market since launching its [Game Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy") in 1989, experiencing close competition only from Sega's [Game Gear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Gear "Game Gear") (1990–1997) and [Bandai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandai "Bandai")'s [WonderSwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WonderSwan "WonderSwan") (1999–2001) and [WonderSwan Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WonderSwan_Color "WonderSwan Color") (2000–2004) in Japan.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-15) In January 1999, Sony released the [PocketStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PocketStation "PocketStation") in Japan as its first foray into the handheld gaming market.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-16) The SNK Neo Geo Pocket and Nokia's N-Gage also failed to cut into Nintendo's share.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-17) According to an [IDC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Data_Corporation "International Data Corporation") analyst in 2004, the PSP was the "first legitimate competitor to Nintendo's dominance in the handheld market".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-18)

The first concept images of the PSP appeared at a Sony corporate strategy meeting in November 2003, and featured a model with flat buttons and no analog joystick.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-19) Although some reviewers expressed concern about the lack of an analog stick,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-20) these fears were allayed when the PSP was officially unveiled at the Sony press conference during [E3 2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2004 "E3 2004").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-IGNPSPFAQ-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-GSE32004-22) Sony released a list of 99 developer companies that pledged support for the new handheld.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-23) Several game demos such as [Konami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konami "Konami")'s _[Metal Gear Acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal\_Gear\_Acid "Metal Gear Acid")_ and [Studio Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Liverpool "Studio Liverpool")'s _[Wipeout Pure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wipeout\_Pure "Wipeout Pure")_ were also shown at the conference.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-24)

The PSP's development posed several challenges for Sony and third-party developers, with battery life being a primary concern. To address this, Sony implemented power management strategies, including restricting the CPU to two-thirds of its full speed for the first few years. The [Universal Media Disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Media_Disc "Universal Media Disc") (UMD) drive was another significant hurdle, as it drained the battery and had slow read speeds. Developers had to optimize their game data layout to minimize disc access and reduce power consumption. These limitations sometimes led to performance constraints and long loading times, with some titles like _[WWE SmackDown! vs. Raw 2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_SmackDown!\_vs.\_Raw\_2006 "WWE SmackDown! vs. Raw 2006")_ experiencing load times of up to two minutes for certain scenes.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-RetroGamer262-25)

### Launch

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Launch")]

On October 18, 2004, Sony announced that the PSP base model would be launched in Japan on December 11 that year for ¥19,800 (about US$181 in 2004) while the Value System would launch for ¥24,800 (about US$226).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-JPlaunchskus-26) The launch was a success, with over 200,000 units sold on the first day of sales.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-27) Color variations were sold in bundle packs that cost around $200. On February 3, 2005, Sony announced that the PSP would be released in North America on March 24 in one configuration for an [MSRP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suggested_retail_price "Suggested retail price") of US$249/CA$299.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-28) Some commentators expressed concern over the high price,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-29) which was almost US$20 higher than that of the Japanese model and over $100 higher than the Nintendo DS.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-30) Despite these concerns, the PSP's North American launch was a success;[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-32) Sony said 500,000 units were sold in the first two days of sales,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-33) though it was also reported that this figure was below expectations.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-34)

The PSP was originally intended to have a simultaneous [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe") and North American launch,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-GSE32004-22) but on March 15, 2005, Sony announced that the European launch would be delayed due to high demand for the console in Japan and North America.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-35) The next month, Sony announced that the PSP would be launched in Europe on September 1, 2005, for €249/£179.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-36) Sony defended the high price by saying North American consumers had to pay local [sales taxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sales_tax "Sales tax") and that the [Value Added Tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Value_Added_Tax "Value Added Tax") (sales tax) was higher in the UK than the US.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-37) Despite the high price, the PSP's launch in Europe was a success, with the console selling over 185,000 units in the UK.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-38) All stock of the PSP in the UK sold out within three hours of its launch, more than doubling the previous first-day sales record of 87,000 units set by the Nintendo DS. The system also enjoyed great success in other areas of Europe; over 25,000 units were pre-ordered in Australia[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-39) and nearly one million units were sold across Europe in the system's first week of sales.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-40)

## Hardware
