#### PSP-1000

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: PSP-1000")]

[![Image 10: Piano Black PSP-1000](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Psp-1000.jpg/250px-Psp-1000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Psp-1000.jpg)

A PSP-1000: the shoulder buttons are on top, the directional pad on the left with the analog stick directly below it, the PlayStation face buttons on the right and a row of secondary buttons below the screen.

The launch model of the PlayStation Portable, referred to as the _PSP-1000_, features an oblong form factor measuring 6.7 by 2.9 by 0.9 inches (170 by 74 by 23 mm). The front of the system features the speakers as well as most of the system's controls, including the face buttons, [d-pad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-pad "D-pad"), and [analog stick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analog_stick "Analog stick"), with other function buttons below the screen. It also contains the system's 4.3-inch (110 mm)[TFT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TFT_LCD "TFT LCD") display, which is capable of 480× 272 pixel display resolution and [24-bit color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24-bit_color "24-bit color"). The top of the system contains the two shoulder buttons, labelled **L** and **R**, the [Wireless LAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_LAN "Wireless LAN") and UMD eject switches, an [IrDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IrDA "IrDA") infrared emitter, and a [Mini USB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini_USB "Mini USB") port for data transfer. Below the system is the AC-in and 2-pin dock ports for charging, as well as the 3.5 mm audio and remote ports. The left and right sides of the system have the [Memory Stick PRO Duo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_Stick_PRO_Duo "Memory Stick PRO Duo") slot and power switch, respectively. The back gives access to the UMD drive and battery slot when either are uncovered. As a whole, the unit weighs 9.9 ounces (280 g).

Internally, the PSP uses two 333[MHz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertz "Hertz")[MIPS32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIPS_architecture "MIPS architecture")[R4000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R4000 "R4000") R4k-based [CPUs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_processing_unit "Central processing unit"), a [GPU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit") running at 166 MHz, and includes 32 MB main [RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_access_memory "Random access memory"), and 4 MB embedded [DRAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_random_access_memory "Dynamic random access memory") split between the GPU and Media Engine.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-SCEAspecs-41) Although the CPU was natively 333 MHz, media would be locked to a maximum of 222 MHz until firmware 3.50 released in May 2007, at which point Sony allowed developers to release new games using higher clock speeds.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-42)

The PSP is powered by an 1800 mAh battery that provides about three to six hours of gameplay, four to five hours of video playback, and eight to eleven hours of audio playback.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-IGNPSPFAQ-21)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-43) The battery completes a full chage after about 1.5 hours.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-44)

### Revisions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Revisions")]

#### PSP-2000

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: PSP-2000")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/PSP_Slim_MS_Slot.JPG/250px-PSP_Slim_MS_Slot.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP_Slim_MS_Slot.JPG)

[Memory Stick PRO Duo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_Stick#Memory_Stick_PRO_Duo "Memory Stick") Slot on a _[Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis\_Core:\_Final\_Fantasy\_VII "Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII")_ edition PSP-2000

At [E3 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2007 "E3 2007"), Sony announced a new revision of the PSP. The PSP-2000, marketed in some regions as "PSP Slim & Lite",[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-45), would first be released in Hong Kong on August 30, 2007, before releasing worldwide in September of that year.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-46) The revision would redesign the system to reduce weight and thickness, from 9.87 to 6.66 ounces (280 to 189 g) and from 0.91 to 0.73 inches (23 to 18.6 mm), respectively.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-SonyE3-47) In addition, the serial port was modified to add video out support, with support for [480i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/480i "480i") output of media via [composite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_video "Composite video"), [S-Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S-Video "S-Video"), [component](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Component_video "Component video"), and [D-Terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-Terminal "D-Terminal"), with the latter two also supporting game output in [480p](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/480p "480p").

Other changes include improved [WLAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_LAN "Wireless LAN") modules, the removal of the IrDA emitter and 2-pin docking port, a simplified UMD drive mechanism, and a thinner,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-48) brighter [LCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_crystal_display "Liquid crystal display") screen. To improve the poor loading times of UMD games on the original PSP,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-49) the internal memory ([RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAM "RAM") and [Flash ROM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_ROM "Flash ROM")) was doubled from 32 MB to 64 MB, part of which now acting as a cache, also improving the web browser's performance.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-gizmodo_specs-50)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Psp-battery-types.jpg/250px-Psp-battery-types.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Psp-battery-types.jpg)

The stock battery included with the PSP-2000 (left) decreased in size and capacity compared to the PSP-1000 battery (right) to maintain a slim form factor.

To make the unit slimmer, the capacity of the PSP's battery was reduced from 1800[mAh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampere_hour "Ampere hour") to 1200 mAh starting with the PSP-2000. The original high-capacity batteries work on newer models, giving increased playing time, though the battery cover does not fit. In March 2008, Sony released the Extended Life Battery Kit in Japan, which included a bulkier 2200 mAh battery with fitting battery covers matching the many PSP variations available.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-51) All versions of the North American kit released in December 2008 were supplied with a black and a silver battery cover.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-52)

#### PSP-3000

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: PSP-3000")]

The PSP-3000 was released in North America on October 14, 2008, in Japan on October 16, in Europe on October 17,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-Gamespot_Release_Article-54) and in Australia on October 23.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-55)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/PSP_3000_Espa%C3%B1ol.jpg/250px-PSP_3000_Espa%C3%B1ol.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP_3000_Espa%C3%B1ol.jpg)

PSP 3000 navigating through [Spanish Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Wikipedia "Spanish Wikipedia")

The PSP-3000, marketed in some areas as "PSP Slim & Lite" or "PSP Brite", was primarily sold as having an improved LCD screen[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-56) with an increased color range,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-57) five times the contrast ratio,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-58) a halved [pixel response time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixel_response_time "Pixel response time"), new sub-pixel structure, and anti-reflective technology to reduce outdoor glare. The disc tray, logos, and buttons were all redesigned, and a microphone was added. Games could now be output in [standard definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_definition "Standard definition") using the [video-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video-in_video-out "Video-in video-out") cable, and more settings were added for the video out, such as flicker reduction, to allow users to tune the video output to their tastes.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-Sony_PSP-3000_Hands-On-59) One outlet called this model "a minor upgrade".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-60)

On its release, the PSP-3000's screen was criticized for what appeared to be scanlines and interlacing artifacts when objects were in motion.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-61) Due to the new screen using horizontal sub-pixels, and the blue sub-pixels appearing less luminant than their red and green counterparts, the blue sub-pixels would create feint horizontal lines across the screen.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-62) Sony stated the issue was inherent to the hardware and would not be fixed.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-63)

In its first four days on sale in Japan, the PSP-3000 sold over 141,270 units, according to _[Famitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famitsu "Famitsu")_;[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-64) it sold 267,000 units during October.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-Japansales-65)

#### PSP Go (N1000)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: PSP Go (N1000)")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/PSP_Go_logo.svg/250px-PSP_Go_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP_Go_logo.svg)

Logo for PSP Go

The PSP Go (model PSP-N1000)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-press_release-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-kotaku_announce-67)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-Announcement-68) was released on October 1, 2009, in North American and European territories,[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-NA/EU_release-69) and on October 31 in Japan. It was revealed prior to [E3 2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2009 "E3 2009") through Sony's [Qore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qore_(PlayStation_Network) "Qore (PlayStation Network)")[video on demand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_on_demand "Video on demand") service.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-joystiq_announce-70) Its design is significantly different from other PSP models.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-kotaku_announce-67)

The unit is 43% lighter and 56% smaller than the original PSP-1000,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-kotaku_announce-67) and 16% lighter and 35% smaller than the PSP-3000.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-TSA-71) Its rechargeable battery is not intended to be removed by the user.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-72) It has a 3.8-inch (97 mm) 480×272 pixel [LCD screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid-crystal_display "Liquid-crystal display"),[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-PlayStation-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-74) which slides up to reveal the main controls. The overall shape and sliding mechanism are similar to those of Sony's [mylo COM-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mylo_(Sony) "Mylo (Sony)") Internet device.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-Giz-75)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/PSP-Go-FL.jpg/250px-PSP-Go-FL.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP-Go-FL.jpg)

Front view of a closed PSP Go

The PSP Go features [802.11b](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IEEE_802.11b-1999 "IEEE 802.11b-1999")[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-76) Wi-Fi like its predecessors, although the [Mini USB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini_USB "Mini USB") port was replaced with an included proprietary connector that handles power, data transfer, and video. [Composite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_video "Composite video") and [component video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Component_video "Component video") cables were sold separately, as well as a [cradle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docking_station "Docking station") that allows both video out and power at the same time.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-press_release-66)[Bluetooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth "Bluetooth") support was also added to the PSP Go, allowing users to connect wireless audio devices and [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3") controllers, the latter officially requires a PS3 system for pairing.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-77)

The PSP Go lacks a UMD drive, instead opting to only 16 GB of internal flash memory.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-Announcement-68) An additional 16 GB can be added with the addition of a [Memory Stick Micro (M2)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_Stick#Memory_Stick_Micro_(M2) "Memory Stick"). Games must be purchased and downloaded from the [PlayStation Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Store "PlayStation Store"). While the PSP Go can download games to itself, users can also download and transfer games to the device from a PlayStation 3 console,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-78) or the [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows")-based software [Media Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_Go "Media Go").

All downloadable PSP and PlayStation games available prior to the model's launch are compatible with the PSP Go. Sony confirmed that almost all UMD-based PSP games released after October 1, 2009, would be available to download[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-79)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-80) and that most older UMD-only games would also be released for digital download in the future.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-81)

The PSP Go sufferred from low consumer interest, with [Kaz Hirai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaz_Hirai "Kaz Hirai") citing the high price point and [piracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_piracy "Digital piracy") as factors for its poor performance.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-82) By February, Sony was considering relaunching the system,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-83)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-84) and began efforts to provide more value to the model. By June of that year, Sony began bundling the console with free downloadable games in certain regions.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-85)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-86)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-87)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-88)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-89) In October 2010, Sony announced the price of the PSP Go would be reduced worldwide, with the American SKU going down to $199.99, from $249.99.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-91) On April 20, 2011, the PSP Go was announced to be discontinued outside of North America to concentrate resources on [PlayStation Vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Vita "PlayStation Vita") manufacturing.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-discon1-92)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-discon2-93)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-discon3-94)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-95)

[![Image 16: PSP-E1000](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/PSP_E1000_illustration.svg/250px-PSP_E1000_illustration.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP_E1000_illustration.svg)

At [Gamescom 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamescom#Gamescom_2011 "Gamescom"), the PSP-E1000, also known as _PSP Street_, was announced as an entry-level PSP system.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-E1000-96) It released exclusively in Europe on October 26, 2011 at a budget price of €99.99.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-97) The E1000 came in a matte finish and lacked support for Wi-Fi, [ad-hoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_ad-hoc_network "Wireless ad-hoc network") features, and stereo audio without headphones.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-98) The brightness button and microphone were also removed, requiring users to enter the system's "Power Save Settings" to adjust the brightness.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-99)

### Bundles and Console Variants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Bundles and Console Variants")]

When PlayStation Portable launched in Japan, it was available either in a standard configuration, which contained the system, battery, and charger, or in the Value Pack, which contained additional accessories, such as a 32 megabyte [Memory Stick Duo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_Stick_Duo "Memory Stick Duo").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-JPlaunchskus-26) When the system launched in North America and Europe, only the Value Pack was available.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-100) Early North American systems were also bundled with the film _[Spider-Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_2 "Spider-Man 2")_ on [UMD Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UMD_Video "UMD Video").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-101) The base configuration as launched in Japan became a standard bundle internationally in 2006.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-102)

Initially, the system was released in "Piano Black", though other color options would come over time, starting with a "Ceramic White" system launching in Japan in September 2005.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-103) At the PSP-2000's launch, multiple color options were available worldwide, including Piano Black, Ceramic White, and Ice Silver.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-104)

Limited edition PSP systems were sold throughout the system's life, usually to promote a bundled game. Some examples of games to get special edition systems include [God of War: Chains of Olympus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_of_War:_Chains_of_Olympus "God of War: Chains of Olympus"), [Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Battlefront:_Renegade_Squadron "Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron"), [Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis_Core:_Final_Fantasy_VII "Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII"), and [Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_Gear_Solid:_Peace_Walker "Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-105)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-106)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-107)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-108) The [Monster Hunter Portable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster_Hunter_Portable "Monster Hunter Portable") Black Golden PSP-3000 system is notable for being physically different from the normal PSP-3000, as it has a concave analog stick and thicker grips to accommodate an Extended Battery pack.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-109)

The PSP Go and E1000 Street models only officially received black and white color variations, with the Pearl White PSP Go only releasing in Japan.

## Software

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Software")]

### System software

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: System software")]

Main article: [PlayStation Portable system software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable_system_software "PlayStation Portable system software")

The PSP runs a custom [operating system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system") referred to as the System Software, which can be updated over the Internet, or by loading an update from a Memory Stick or UMD.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-SYSupdate-112) Sony does not provide a method to perform operating system downgrades.

While System Software updates can be used with consoles from any region,[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-113) Sony recommends only downloading updates released for the model's region. System Software updates have added many features, including a web browser, [Adobe Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Flash_Player "Adobe Flash Player") support, additional codecs for various media, [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3") (PS3) connectivity, and patches against security exploits and the execution of [homebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homebrew_(video_games) "Homebrew (video games)") programs.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-SYSupdate-112) The most recent version, numbered 6.61, was released on January 15, 2015.

### Apps and functionality

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Apps and functionality")]

#### Web browser

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Web browser")]

See also: [PlayStation Portable system software §Web browser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable_system_software#Web_browser "PlayStation Portable system software")

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/PSP_Browser.jpg/250px-PSP_Browser.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP_Browser.jpg)

Web browser on a PSP-1000

The PSP Internet Browser is a version of the [NetFront](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NetFront "NetFront") browser and came with the system via the 2.00 update.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-114) The browser supports most common web technologies, such as [HTTP cookies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_cookie "HTTP cookie"), [forms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Form_(web) "Form (web)"), [CSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascading_Style_Sheets "Cascading Style Sheets"), and basic [JavaScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript "JavaScript").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-115) It features basic [tabbed browsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabbed_document_interface "Tabbed document interface") and has a maximum of three tabs.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-116)

#### Remote Play

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Remote Play")]

Main article: [Remote Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remote_Play "Remote Play")

Remote Play allows the PSP to access many of the features of the PlayStation 3 console from a remote location using the PS3's [WLAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_LAN "Wireless LAN") capabilities, a home network, or the Internet.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-117) Using Remote Play, users can view photographs, listen to music, and watch videos stored on the PS3 or connected USB devices.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-aboutRP-118) Remote Play also allows the PS3 to be turned on and off remotely and lets the PSP control audio playback from the PS3 to a home theater system.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-119)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-120) Although most of the PS3's capabilities are accessible with Remote Play, playback of [DVDs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD"), Blu-ray Discs, [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)") games, PlayStation 2 games, most PS3 games, and [copy-protected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copy_protection "Copy protection") files stored on the hard drive are not supported.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-aboutRP-118)

#### VoIP access

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: VoIP access")]

Starting with System Software version 3.90, the PSP-2000, 3000, and Go could use the [Skype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skype "Skype")[VoIP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VoIP "VoIP") service. Due to hardware constraints it was not possible to use the service on the PSP-1000. The service allowed Skype calls to be made over Wi-Fi and– on the Go– over the Bluetooth modem. Users had to purchase Skype credit to make telephone calls.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-skype1-121) Skype for PlayStation Portable was discontinued on June 22, 2016.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-122)

#### Room for PlayStation Portable

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Room for PlayStation Portable")]

Main article: [Room for PlayStation Portable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room_for_PlayStation_Portable "Room for PlayStation Portable")

At [Tokyo Game Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Game_Show "Tokyo Game Show") 2009, Sony announced that a service similar to [PlayStation Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Home "PlayStation Home"), the PS3's online community-based service, was being developed for the PSP.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-123) Named "Room" (stylized _R∞M_), it was being [beta-tested](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_testing "Beta testing") in Japan from October 2009 to April 2010. It could be launched directly from the PlayStation Network section of the [XMB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XMB "XMB"). As in Home, PSP owners would have been able to invite other PSP owners into their rooms to "enjoy real time communication".[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-124)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-125) Development of Room halted on April 15, 2010, due to feedback from the community.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-126)

#### SensMe application

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: SensMe application")]

The [SensMe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SensMe "SensMe") software, which had already existed on some [Walkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkman "Walkman") music players and [Sony Ericsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Ericsson "Sony Ericsson") handsets, was added to the PSP through a software update in 2009. It is a music analyser that reads music files stored on the PSP and categorises them into "channels" representing moods and creates automatic playlists from it.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-127)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-128) The PSP has support for the playback of [MP3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MP3 "MP3") and [ATRAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATRAC "ATRAC") audio files,[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-129) as well as [WMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Media_Audio "Windows Media Audio") since firmware version 2.60.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-130)

#### Digital Comics Reader

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Digital Comics Reader")]

Sony partnered with publishers such as [Rebellion Developments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebellion_Developments "Rebellion Developments"), [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney"), [IDW Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDW_Publishing "IDW Publishing"), [Insomnia Publications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insomnia_Publications "Insomnia Publications"), [iVerse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IVerse?action=edit&redlink=1 "IVerse (page does not exist)"), [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics"), and [Titan Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titan_Books "Titan Books") to release digitized comics on the PlayStation Store.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-131)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-132) The Digital Comics Reader application required PSP firmware 6.20.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-133)

The PlayStation Store's "Comic" section premiered in Japan on December 10, 2009, with licensed publishers [ASCII Media Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCII_Media_Works "ASCII Media Works"), [Enterbrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enterbrain "Enterbrain"), [Kadokawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kadokawa_Shoten "Kadokawa Shoten"), [Kodansha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kodansha "Kodansha"), [Shueisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shueisha "Shueisha"), [Shogakukan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shogakukan "Shogakukan"), [Square-Enix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square-Enix "Square-Enix"), [Softbank Creative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softbank_Creative "Softbank Creative") (HQ Comics), [Hakusensha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hakusensha "Hakusensha"), [Bandai Visual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandai_Visual "Bandai Visual"), Fujimishobo, [Futabasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Futabasha "Futabasha"), and Bunkasha.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-134) It launched in the United States and in English-speaking PAL countries on December 16, 2009, though the first issues of _Aleister Arcane_, _[Astro Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro\_Boy "Astro Boy"): Movie Adaptation_, _[Star Trek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Trek "Star Trek"): Enterprise Experiment_ and _[Transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers "Transformers"): All Hail Megatron_ were made available as early as November 20 through limited-time PlayStation Network redemption codes.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-135) In early 2010 the application was expanded to the German, French, Spanish and Italian languages.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-136) The choice of regional Comic Reader software is dictated by the PSP's firmware region; the Japanese Comic Reader will not display comics purchased from the European store, and vice versa. Sony shut down the Digital Comics service in September 2012.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-137)

#### x-Radar Portable

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: x-Radar Portable")]

In Japanese market PSPs, the application x-Radar Portable was preloaded starting with firmware version 6.35 (January 2010). This is a port of a map software for PCs and mobile phones called x-Radar, developed by PetaMap. x-Radar Portable finds the location of the PSP on a map and obtains information of places near the user. It determines the location through "PlaceEngine" technology, via wireless LAN spots.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-138)

### Homebrew development and custom firmware

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Homebrew development and custom firmware")]

Main articles: [PlayStation Portable homebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable_homebrew "PlayStation Portable homebrew") and [Custom firmware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Custom_firmware "Custom firmware")

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/PSP-Homebrew.jpeg/250px-PSP-Homebrew.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP-Homebrew.jpeg)

Metallic Blue PSP 1000 running a ["Hello, World!" program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22Hello,_World!%22_program "\"Hello, World!\" program")

On June 15, 2005, hackers disassembled the code of the PSP and distributed it online.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-139) Initially the modified PSP allowed users to run custom code and a limited amount of protected software, including custom-made PSP applications such as a calculator or file manager.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-140) Sony responded to this by repeatedly upgrading the software. Some users were able to unlock the [firmware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firmware "Firmware") to allow them to run more custom content and [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management "Digital rights management")-restricted software. Hackers were able to run protected software on the PSP through the creation of ISO loaders that could load copies of UMD games from a memory stick.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-141)[Custom firmware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Custom_firmware "Custom firmware") including the M33 Custom Firmware, Minimum Edition (ME/LME) CFW and PRO CFW were commonly seen in PSP systems.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-142)

### Content management

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Content management")]

The management of media content of the PSP through personal computers was fulfilled by Sony's [PSP Media Manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSP_Media_Manager "PSP Media Manager") software for Windows, allowing transfer as well as music/video playback and backups.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-143) In 2009 the PSP Media Manager was replaced by [Media Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_Go "Media Go").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-144)

## Games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Games")]

See also: [List of PlayStation Portable games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_PlayStation_Portable_games "List of PlayStation Portable games"), [List of downloadable PlayStation Portable games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_downloadable_PlayStation_Portable_games "List of downloadable PlayStation Portable games"), [List of best-selling PSP video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_PSP_video_games "List of best-selling PSP video games"), and [List of cancelled PlayStation Portable video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cancelled_PlayStation_Portable_video_games "List of cancelled PlayStation Portable video games")

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/UMDDISCK.JPG/250px-UMDDISCK.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UMDDISCK.JPG)

A typical PSP game, on a [Universal Media Disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Media_Disc "Universal Media Disc")

Worldwide, there were 1,370 games released for the PSP between 2004 and 2016. At launch, all games were strictly released on [UMD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Univeral_Media_Disc "Univeral Media Disc"), but in October 2008, the [PlayStation Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Store "PlayStation Store") would launch for PSP.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-145) By 2009, Sony started the [PlayStation mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_mini "PlayStation mini") line of games, which were smaller-scale digital-only PSP games, and promised all future major releases on UMD would come digitally.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-146)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-147)

In addition to standard PlayStation Portable software, digitally released [PSone Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSone_Classics "PSone Classics") also became playable on PSP via firmware 3.00, though they needed to be installed from a [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3") system until the PlayStation Store launched on PSP.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-148) In 2009, [Turbografx-16 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_PlayStation_Store_TurboGrafx-16_games "List of PlayStation Store TurboGrafx-16 games") were also added to the PlayStation Store.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-149)

The best selling PSP game is _[Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto:\_Liberty\_City\_Stories "Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories")_, which has sold 7.5 million copies as of July 20, 2013.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-150) Other top selling PSP games include _[Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto:\_Vice\_City\_Stories "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories")_,[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-151)_[Monster Hunter Portable 3rd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_Hunter\_Portable\_3rd "Monster Hunter Portable 3rd")_,[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-CapcomPlanet-152)_[Gran Turismo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran\_Turismo\_(2009\_video\_game) "Gran Turismo (2009 video game)")_,[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-153) and _[Monster Hunter Freedom Unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_Hunter\_Freedom\_Unite "Monster Hunter Freedom Unite")_.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-CapcomPlanet-152) The final physical UMD release in North America was _[Summon Night 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summon\_Night\_5 "Summon Night 5")_ in April 2016, with _[Retro City Rampage DX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro\_City\_Rampage\_DX "Retro City Rampage DX")_ following as the final digital release in July 2016.

During [E3 2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2006 "E3 2006"), Sony Computer Entertainment America announced that the [Greatest Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Sony_Greatest_Hits_games "List of Sony Greatest Hits games") range of budget titles were to be extended to the PSP system with games in the line retailing for $19.99.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-154) On July 25, 2006, Sony Computer Entertainment America released the first batch of Greatest Hits titles including _[Ape Escape: On the Loose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ape\_Escape:\_On\_the\_Loose "Ape Escape: On the Loose")_, _[ATV Offroad Fury: Blazin' Trails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATV\_Offroad\_Fury:\_Blazin'\_Trails "ATV Offroad Fury: Blazin' Trails")_, _[Hot Shots: Open Tee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody's\_Golf#Everybody's\_Golf "Everybody's Golf")_, _[Twisted Metal: Head-On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twisted\_Metal:\_Head-On "Twisted Metal: Head-On")_, and _[Wipeout Pure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wipeout\_Pure "Wipeout Pure")_.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-GHpress-155)

[Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_trophies "PlayStation trophies") support was planned for the PSP but the idea was cancelled after the firmware was cracked, as Sony feared that hacked systems could allow players to illegitimately unlock or manipulate trophies.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-156)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-157)

### Demos and emulation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Demos and emulation")]

In late 2004, Sony released a series of PSP demo games, including _Duck In Water_, _world/ball_, _Harmonic City_, and _Luga City_.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-158) Demos for commercial PSP games could be downloaded and booted directly from a [Memory Stick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_Stick "Memory Stick").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-159) Demos were sometimes issued in UMD format and mailed out or given to customers at retail outlets.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-160) In addition, several older [PlayStation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_(console) "PlayStation (console)") games were re-released; these can be played on the PSP using [emulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_console_emulator "Video game console emulator"). As of 2008[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit), this feature could be officially accessed through the [PlayStation Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Network "PlayStation Network") service for [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3"), PSP, [PlayStation Vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Vita "PlayStation Vita") (or [PlayStation TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_TV "PlayStation TV")), or a [personal computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer "Personal computer").[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-161)[Emulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_console_emulator "Video game console emulator") of the PSP is well-developed; the first emulator was [pspplayer by Noxa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pspplayer_by_Noxa?action=edit&redlink=1 "Pspplayer by Noxa (page does not exist)"), which ran on C#, then afterwards was [JPCSP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JPCSP?action=edit&redlink=1 "JPCSP (page does not exist)") which ran on [Java](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_(programming_language) "Java (programming language)").[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-162)[PPSSPP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PPSSPP "PPSSPP") is currently the fastest and most compatible PSP emulator; it supports all major games.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-163)

### Data installation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Data installation")]

In mid 2009,[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-164) as larger memory stick storage became available for the PSP, the ability to pre-install some or all data from a game became a feature in certain games. Although for a large majority of the games the feature merely improved load times, there were a small number of games that added features, such as voice acting in Codec conversations in _[Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal\_Gear\_Solid:\_Peace\_Walker "Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker")_.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-165)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Reception")]

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/PSP_and_DS.jpg/250px-PSP_and_DS.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSP_and_DS.jpg)

PlayStation Portable (top) and Nintendo DS (bottom). All of the screens are [fogged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fogging_(censorship) "Fogging (censorship)") out.

The PSP received generally positive reviews soon after launch; most reviewers noted similar strengths and weaknesses. _[CNET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNET "CNET")_ awarded the system 8.5 out of 10 and praised the console's powerful hardware and its multimedia capabilities but lamented the lack of a guard to cover the screen and the reading surface of UMD cartridges.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-170)_[Engadget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engadget "Engadget")_ praised the console's design, stating that "it is definitely one well-designed, slick little handheld".[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-171)_[PC World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PC\_World "PC World")_ commended the built-in Wi-Fi capability but criticized the lack of a web browser at launch, and the glare and smudges that resulted from the console's glossy exterior.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-172) Most reviewers also praised the console's large, bright viewing screen and its audio and video playback capabilities. In 2008, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ listed the PSP as a "gotta have travel gadget", citing the console's movie selection, telecommunications capability, and upcoming GPS functionality.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-173)

The PlayStation Portable was initially seen as superior to the Nintendo DS when both devices were revealed in early 2004 because of the designers' emphasis on the technical accomplishments of the system. Nintendo of America President [Reggie Fils-Aime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Fils-Aime "Reggie Fils-Aime"), however, focused on the experience aspect of the Nintendo DS.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-eurgm-174) The DS started to become more popular than the PSP early on because it attracted more third-party developers, and appealed more to the casual gaming market. The DS sold more units partly because of its touchscreen and second display.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-nlffe-175)

## Marketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=PlayStation_Portable&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Marketing")]

In late 2005, Sony said it had hired graffiti artists to spray-paint advertisements for the PSP in seven major U.S. cities, including New York City, Atlanta, Philadelphia, and San Francisco. According to Sony, it was paying businesses and building owners for the right to spray-paint their walls.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-214) A year later, Sony ran a poster campaign in England; a poster bearing the slogan "Take a running jump here" was removed from a [Manchester Piccadilly station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Piccadilly_station "Manchester Piccadilly station") tram platform due to concerns it might encourage suicide.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-215)

Later in 2006, news of a billboard advertisement released in the Netherlands depicting a white woman holding a black woman by the jaw, saying "PlayStation Portable White is coming", spread. Two similar advertisements existed; one showed the two women facing each other on equal footing in fighting stances, the other showed the black woman in a dominant position on top of the white woman. Sony's stated purpose was to contrast the white and black versions of the PSP, but the advertisements were interpreted as being racially charged. These advertisements were never released in the rest of the world and were withdrawn from the Netherlands after the controversy.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-cnn-216) The advertisement attracted international press coverage; Engadget said Sony may have hoped to "capitalize on a PR firestorm".[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-217)

Sony came under scrutiny online in December 2006 for a [guerrilla marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_marketing "Guerrilla marketing") campaign in which advertisers posed as young bloggers who desperately wanted a PSP. The site, alliwantforxmasisapsp.com, appeared to have been designed by two friends and featured downloadable PSP greetings cards and t-shirt transfers. It also hosted a video showing "Cousin Pete" rapping about the handheld. The authors described the blog as "Consider us your own personal psp hype machine, here to help you wage a holiday assault on ur parents, girl, granny, boss - whoever - so they know what you really want,".[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-218) The blog entries were written in a mixture of "leetspeak" and "smacktard". "i (charlie) have a psp. my friend jeremy does not. but he wants one this year for xmas," fake authors "c&j" wrote, "so we started clowning with sum not-so-subtle hints to j's parents that a psp would be teh perfect gift. we created this site to spread the luv to those like j who want a psp!"[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-219) Additionally, the blog author also uploaded a video of a guy rapping about wanting a PSP for Christmas.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-220) Sony and Zipatoni were outed on the blog itself by tech-savvy critics who reportedly found the blog's registration data through an online search, and tracked it back to Gregory Meyerkord at advertising firm [Zipatoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipatoni?action=edit&redlink=1 "Zipatoni (page does not exist)").[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-221)

At [E3 2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3_2010 "E3 2010"), Sony created a fictional 12-year-old character that was used by [Sony Computer Entertainment America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Computer_Entertainment_America "Sony Computer Entertainment America") as part of their _Step Your Game Up_ advertising campaign for the PlayStation Portable and [PSPgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSPgo "PSPgo") consoles in North America, as part of the [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3")'s "It Only Does Everything" advertising campaign.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-Marcus_is_Kevin_for_PSP-222) The character, Marcus Rivers, was played by child-actor [Bobb'e J. Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobb'e_J._Thompson "Bobb'e J. Thompson"), and started as the publicist of the PlayStation Portable division of Sony, responding to "Dear PSP" queries.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-223) Marcus was additionally used to advertise games for the system.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-224) The character was eventually discontinued due to his negative reception, with the "Dear PSP" campaign continuing without them.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Portable#cite_note-225)
